title.raw: 卷三十二 列傳第二十二 張邵 Volume 32 Biographies 22: Zhang Shao

sentences.zh: 列傳第二十二

translations.literal: Biographies 22
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 22

sentences.zh: 桓玄篡位，父敞先為尚書，以答事微謬，降為廷尉卿。

translations.literal: When Huan Xuan usurped the throne, Shao's father Chang had previously served as Minister of the Interior; for a minor error in handling correspondence he was demoted to Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: After Huan Xuan seized the throne, Shao's father Chang, who had served as minister of the interior, was demoted to minister of justice over a small mistake in official paperwork.

sentences.zh: 及宋武帝討桓玄，邵白敞表獻忠款，帝大悅，命署寺門曰：「有犯張廷尉家者，軍法論。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Song marched against Huan Xuan, Shao had Chang submit a memorial pledging loyalty; the Emperor was greatly pleased and ordered posted at the ministry gate: "Anyone who violates the household of Minister of Justice Chang shall be punished by military law.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yu marched against Huan Xuan, Shao had his father submit a memorial of loyalty. Delighted, the emperor ordered posted at the ministry gate: "Anyone who harms Minister of Justice Chang's household will be dealt with by military law.

sentences.zh: 」事平，以敞為吳郡太守。

translations.literal: " After the affair was settled, Chang was appointed Governor of Wu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: " Once the rebellion was crushed, Chang was made governor of Wu Commandery.

sentences.zh: 及王謐為揚州，召邵補主簿。

translations.literal: When Wang Mi became governor of Yang Province, he summoned Shao to serve as chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Mi took charge of Yang Province, he called Shao in as chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 劉毅位居亞相，好士愛才，當世莫不輻湊，唯邵不往。

translations.literal: Liu Yi held the second rank among ministers, loved scholars and prized talent, and men of the age flocked to him—only Shao did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yi ranked just below the chief minister, loved scholars, and drew every ambitious man of the age—except Shao, who never visited.

sentences.zh: 親故怪而問之，邵曰：「主公命世人傑，何煩多問。

translations.literal: Relatives and friends wondered and asked him; Shao said, "Our lord is a hero of the age—why trouble with so many questions?
translations.idiomatic: Kinsmen and friends asked why; Shao replied, "Our master is a hero of the age. Why pester him with needless questions?

sentences.zh: 」劉穆之言於帝，帝益親之，轉太尉參軍，署長流賊曹。

translations.literal: " Liu Muzhi spoke of this to the Emperor, who grew still closer to Shao, transferred him to staff secretary of the grand commandant, and assigned him to the bureau of river-bandits and long-distance fugitives.
translations.idiomatic: " Liu Muzhi told the emperor, who drew Shao closer still, made him a staff secretary under the grand commandant, and put him in charge of river-bandits and long-distance fugitives.

sentences.zh: 盧循至蔡洲，武帝至石頭，使邵守南城。

translations.literal: When Lu Xun reached Caizhou, the Emperor came to Shitou and had Shao hold the southern city.
translations.idiomatic: When Lu Xun reached Caizhou, Liu Yu came to Shitou and left Shao to defend the southern wall.

sentences.zh: 時百姓水際望賊，帝不解其意，以問邵。

translations.literal: At that time common people along the water watched the bandits; the Emperor did not understand their intent and asked Shao.
translations.idiomatic: People along the riverbank were watching the enemy camp; the emperor did not understand why and asked Shao.

sentences.zh: 邵曰：「節鉞未反，奔散之不暇，亦何暇觀望，今當無復恐耳。

translations.literal: Shao said, "Since the command baton has not yet returned, they have no leisure to scatter—much less to stand and stare; now there should be no further fear.
translations.idiomatic: Shao said, "The command baton has not come back yet, so they are too busy to flee—let alone gawk. Their fear should be over now.

sentences.zh: 」帝以邵勤練憂公，重補州主簿。

translations.literal: " The Emperor, seeing Shao's diligence and public-mindedness, again appointed him chief clerk of the province.
translations.idiomatic: " Impressed by Shao's tireless devotion to duty, the emperor reappointed him provincial chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 邵悉心政事，精力絕人，及誅劉藩，邵時在西州直廬，即夜誡眾曹曰：「大軍當大討，可各各條倉庫及舟船人領，至曉取辦。

translations.literal: Shao gave himself wholly to administration with energy beyond ordinary men; when Liu Fan was executed, Shao was then on night duty in the western office and that very night admonished all the bureaus: "The great army is about to launch a major campaign—each of you should itemize the storehouses, boats, ships, and personnel rolls; by dawn have everything ready.
translations.idiomatic: Shao threw himself into governance with extraordinary energy. On the night Liu Fan was executed, Shao was on night duty in the western office and immediately warned every bureau: "A major campaign is coming. List every warehouse, boat, ship, and roster of personnel—have it all ready by dawn.

sentences.zh: 」旦日，帝求諸簿最，應時即至，怪問其速。

translations.literal: " At dawn the Emperor asked for the registers and they were delivered at once; surprised, he asked how it was so fast.
translations.idiomatic: " At daybreak the emperor demanded the registers and they appeared instantly. Astonished, he asked how they were ready so quickly.

sentences.zh: 諸曹答曰：「宿受張主簿處分。

translations.literal: The bureaus answered, "We received Chief Clerk Zhang's orders overnight.
translations.idiomatic: The clerks answered, "Chief Clerk Zhang gave us our orders last night.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「張邵可謂同人憂慮矣。」

translations.literal: " The Emperor said, "Zhang Shao may truly be said to share the cares of his fellows."
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "Zhang Shao truly shares the burden with his colleagues."

sentences.zh: 九年，世子始開徵虜府，以邵補錄事參軍，轉號中軍，遷諮議參軍，領記室。

translations.literal: In the ninth year the heir apparent first opened the Pacification-of-Captives headquarters; Shao was appointed recording secretary, then transferred to the central army, promoted to advisory secretary, and put in charge of the secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year the heir opened the Pacification-of-Captives headquarters. Shao became recording secretary, then moved to the central army, rose to advisory secretary, and headed the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 十一年，武帝北伐，邵請見曰：「人生危脆，宜有遠慮。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, on the Emperor's northern campaign, Shao requested an audience and said, "Human life is fragile—one should plan far ahead.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year, before the northern campaign, Shao asked to see the emperor and said, "Life is fragile. You should plan for the distant future.

sentences.zh: 若劉穆之邂逅不幸，誰可代之？

translations.literal: If Liu Muzhi should meet with sudden misfortune, who could replace him?
translations.idiomatic: If Liu Muzhi were to die unexpectedly, who could take his place?

sentences.zh: 尊業如此，若有不諱，則處分雲何？

translations.literal: Your great enterprise is at such a point—if the unthinkable happened, how would affairs be ordered?
translations.idiomatic: Your enterprise stands at its height—if the worst befell you, how would the realm be governed?

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「此自委穆之與卿耳。」

translations.literal: " The Emperor said, "That I leave to Muzhi and to you."
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor answered, "I leave that to Muzhi—and to you."

sentences.zh: 青州刺史檀祗鎮廣陵，輒率眾至滁中掩討亡命，劉穆之慮其為變，議欲遣軍。

translations.literal: Tan Zhi, governor of Qing Province, was stationed at Guangling and on his own authority led troops to Chuzhong to strike down fugitives; Liu Muzhi feared he might rebel and debated sending troops against him.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Zhi, governor of Qing Province, garrisoned at Guangling and on his own authority marched to Chuzhong to hunt fugitives. Liu Muzhi feared a mutiny and considered sending troops.

sentences.zh: 邵曰：「檀韶據中流，道濟為軍首，若有相疑之跡，則大府立危。

translations.literal: Shao said, "Tan Shao holds the midstream and Tan Daoji leads the army—if there were any sign of mutual suspicion, the grand headquarters would be in immediate peril.
translations.idiomatic: Shao said, "Tan Shao holds the midstream and Tan Daoji commands the army. Any hint of mutual suspicion would put the grand headquarters in instant danger.

sentences.zh: 不如逆遣慰勞，必無患也。

translations.literal: Better to send envoys ahead with words of comfort—there will certainly be no trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Send envoys ahead with words of reassurance instead—there will be no trouble.

sentences.zh: 」祗果不動。

translations.literal: " Tan Zhi indeed did not move.
translations.idiomatic: " Tan Zhi did not stir.

sentences.zh: 及穆之暴卒，朝廷恇懼，便發詔以司馬徐羨之代之。

translations.literal: When Muzhi died suddenly, the court was terrified and at once issued an edict appointing Marshal Xu Xianzhi to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: When Muzhi died suddenly, the court panicked and immediately issued an edict naming Marshal Xu Xianzhi as his successor.

sentences.zh: 邵獨曰：「今誠急病，任終在徐；

translations.literal: Shao alone said, "The emergency is real and the charge will end with Xu;
translations.idiomatic: Shao alone objected: "This is a true emergency, and Xu will ultimately bear the charge;

sentences.zh: 然世子無專行之義，宜須諮。

translations.literal: yet the heir has no authority to act on his own—he must be consulted.
translations.idiomatic: but the heir has no right to act alone. He must be consulted first.

sentences.zh: 」信反，方使世子出命曰：「朝廷及大府事悉諮徐司馬，其餘啟還。

translations.literal: " When the messenger returned, only then did they have the heir issue orders: "All court and grand-headquarters business is to be referred to Marshal Xu; other memorials are to be sent back.
translations.idiomatic: " When the messenger returned, the heir was made to order: "All court and headquarters business goes to Marshal Xu; everything else comes back to me.

sentences.zh: 」武帝善其臨事不撓，得大臣節。

translations.literal: " The Emperor approved his unwavering conduct in crisis and said he had the bearing of a great minister.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor praised his steadiness under pressure and said he had shown a great minister's resolve.

sentences.zh: 十四年，世子改授荊州，邵諫曰：「儲貳之重，四海所系，不宜外出，敢以死請。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year the heir was reassigned to Jing Province; Shao remonstrated: "The weight of the heir apparent binds the four seas—it is not fitting that he go abroad; I dare beg this at the cost of my life.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year the heir was reassigned to Jing Province. Shao protested: "The heir apparent holds the realm together. He must not leave the capital. I beg this even at the cost of my life.

sentences.zh: 」世子竟不行。

translations.literal: " The heir in the end did not go.
translations.idiomatic: " In the end the heir did not go.

sentences.zh: 文帝為中郎將、荊州刺史，以邵為司馬，領南郡相，眾事悉決于邵。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen was middle general and governor of Jing Province, he made Shao marshal and concurrently administrator of Nan Commandery; all affairs were decided by Shao.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen was middle general and governor of Jing Province, he made Shao his marshal and concurrent administrator of Nan Commandery, leaving all business to him.

sentences.zh: 武帝受命，以佐命功封臨沮伯。

translations.literal: When the Emperor received the Mandate, Shao was enfeoffed as Baron of Linju for his merit in establishing the dynasty.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yu took the throne, Shao was enfeoffed as Baron of Linju for helping establish the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 分荊州立湘州，以邵為刺史，將署府，邵以長沙內地，非用武之國，置府妨人，乖為政要。

translations.literal: When Xiang Province was split from Jing Province, Shao was made its governor; about to set up his headquarters, he argued that the interior of Changsha was no country for military camps and that establishing offices would harm the people and violate the essentials of governance.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiang Province was carved from Jing Province, Shao was named governor. About to establish his headquarters, he argued that inland Changsha was no place for a military camp and that setting up offices would burden the people and betray good governance.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: They assented.
translations.idiomatic: They agreed.

sentences.zh: 荊州刺史謝晦反，遺書要邵，邵不發函，使呈文帝。

translations.literal: When Jing Province Governor Xie Hui rebelled, he sent a letter summoning Shao; Shao did not break the seal but had it presented to Emperor Wen.
translations.idiomatic: When Xie Hui, governor of Jing Province, rebelled, he sent a letter summoning Shao. Shao left the seal unbroken and had it shown to Emperor Wen.

sentences.zh: 元嘉五年，轉征虜將軍，領甯蠻校尉、雍州刺史，加都督。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yuanjia he was transferred to General Who Pacifies the Barbarians, concurrently Colonel Who Pacifies the Man, and Governor of Yong Province, with added area command.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanjia 5 he became general who pacifies the barbarians, colonel who pacifies the Man, and governor of Yong Province, with area command added.

sentences.zh: 初，王華與邵不和，及華參要，親舊為之危心。

translations.literal: At first Wang Hua and Shao were not on good terms; when Hua joined the inner council, kinsmen and friends worried for Shao.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hua and Shao had once been at odds; when Hua entered the inner council, friends feared for Shao.

sentences.zh: 邵曰：「子陵方弘至公，豈以私隙害正義。

translations.literal: Shao said, "Ziling is now pursuing the utmost public good—how could he harm justice over a private grudge?
translations.idiomatic: Shao said, "Ziling now pursues the public good. He would not let a private quarrel override justice.

sentences.zh: 」是任也，華實舉之。

translations.literal: " In this appointment, Hua had in fact recommended him.
translations.idiomatic: " Hua had in fact recommended him for the post.

sentences.zh: 及至襄陽，築長圍，修立堤堰，創田數千頃，公私充給。

translations.literal: On reaching Xiangyang he built long encirclements, repaired dikes and sluices, and opened several thousand qing of fields; public and private stores were filled.
translations.idiomatic: At Xiangyang he built long siege lines, repaired dikes and sluices, and opened thousands of qing of farmland until public and private stores overflowed.

sentences.zh: 丹、淅二川蠻屢為寇，邵誘其帥並出，因大會誅之，遣軍掩其村落，悉禽。

translations.literal: The barbarians of the Dan and Xi rivers repeatedly raided; Shao lured their chiefs to come out together, then at a great assembly executed them and sent troops to overrun their villages, capturing all.
translations.idiomatic: Tribes along the Dan and Xi repeatedly raided. Shao lured their chiefs to a gathering, executed them at the feast, then sent troops to overrun their villages and capture everyone.

sentences.zh: 既失信群蠻，所在並起，水陸路斷。

translations.literal: Having broken faith with the barbarian peoples, uprisings broke out everywhere and land and water routes were cut.
translations.idiomatic: Having betrayed the tribes, he faced revolts everywhere; land and water routes were severed.

sentences.zh: 七年，子敷至襄陽定省，當還都，群蠻欲斷取之，會蠕蠕國獻使下，蠻以為是敷，因掠之。

translations.literal: In the seventh year his son Fu came to Xiangyang on a family visit and was to return to the capital; the tribes meant to intercept and seize him, but an envoy from the Rouran arrived downstream and the tribes, thinking it was Fu, plundered the envoy instead.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year his son Fu visited Xiangyang and was returning to court when tribesmen meant to seize him. A Rouran envoy came downriver; mistaking him for Fu, they robbed the envoy instead.

sentences.zh: 邵坐降號揚烈將軍。

translations.literal: Shao was demoted in rank to General of Yang Might.
translations.idiomatic: Shao was demoted to general of yang might.

sentences.zh: 江夏王義恭鎮江陵，以邵為撫軍長史、持節、南蠻校尉。

translations.literal: When Prince of Jiangxia Yigong was stationed at Jiangling, he made Shao chief secretary of the pacification army, with credential-bearing staff and colonel of the southern barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Yigong of Jiangxia held Jiangling, he made Shao chief secretary of the pacification army, with credential staff and the title colonel of the southern barbarians.

sentences.zh: 九年，坐在雍州營私畜取贓貨二百四十五萬，下廷尉，免官削爵土。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was charged with in Yong Province privately amassing goods and taking bribes worth 2,450,000; sent to the minister of justice, he was dismissed and stripped of rank and fief.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was accused of privately hoarding goods and taking bribes worth 2,450,000 in Yong Province. Tried by the minister of justice, he was dismissed and stripped of rank and fief.

sentences.zh: 後為吳興太守，卒。

translations.literal: Later he served as governor of Wuxing and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as governor of Wuxing and died in office.

sentences.zh: 追復爵邑，諡曰簡伯。

translations.literal: Posthumously his title and fief were restored and he was given the posthumous name Baron Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously his title and fief were restored and he was given the posthumous name Jian.

sentences.zh: 邵臨終遺命，祭以菜果，葦席為車需車，諸子從焉。

translations.literal: On his deathbed Shao left instructions that sacrifices be made with vegetables and fruit, with reed mats for carriage fittings; his sons followed this.
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed Shao ordered that his rites use only vegetables and fruit, with reed mats for the hearse; his sons obeyed.

sentences.zh: 長子敷。

translations.literal: His eldest son was Fu.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son was Fu.

sentences.zh: 敷字景胤，生而母亡。

translations.literal: Fu, styled Jingyin, lost his mother at birth.
translations.idiomatic: Fu, styled Jingyin, lost his mother at birth.

sentences.zh: 年數歲問知之，雖童蒙便有感慕之色。

translations.literal: At a few years of age he asked and learned of it; though still a child he already showed the look of longing and grief.
translations.idiomatic: When he was only a few years old he learned what had happened; even as a small child his face showed longing and grief.

sentences.zh: 至十歲許，求母遺物，而散施已盡，唯得一扇，乃緘錄之。

translations.literal: By about ten he sought his mother's belongings, but they had all been given away; he obtained only a fan, which he sealed and kept.
translations.idiomatic: Around ten he searched for his mother's belongings, but everything had been given away except a fan, which he sealed away and kept.

sentences.zh: 每至感思，輒開笥流涕。

translations.literal: Whenever grief came over him he would open the chest and weep.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever longing overwhelmed him he opened the chest and wept.

sentences.zh: 見從母，悲感哽咽。

translations.literal: Seeing his mother's sister, he would choke with sorrow.
translations.idiomatic: At the sight of his mother's sister he would choke with sorrow.

sentences.zh: 性整貴，風韻甚高，好讀玄言，兼屬文論。

translations.literal: By nature he was upright and noble, with bearing of the highest refinement; he loved reading Dark Learning texts and also composed literary essays.
translations.idiomatic: Upright and noble by nature, with the highest refinement of bearing, he loved Dark Learning and wrote essays as well.

sentences.zh: 初，父邵使與高士南陽宗少文談系象，往復數番。

translations.literal: At first his father Shao had him discuss the patterns of the cosmos with the recluse Zong Shaowen of Nanyang; they exchanged several rounds.
translations.idiomatic: Early on his father had him debate cosmic patterns with the recluse Zong Shaowen of Nanyang; they went back and forth several times.

sentences.zh: 少文每欲屈，握麈尾歎曰：「吾道東矣。

translations.literal: Shaowen, wanting to yield each time, would grasp his fly-whisk and sigh: "My Way has gone east.
translations.idiomatic: Shaowen, about to concede each time, would grip his fly-whisk and sigh: "My Way has gone east.

sentences.zh: 」於是名價日重。

translations.literal: " From then on his fame grew daily.
translations.idiomatic: " From then his reputation rose daily.

sentences.zh: 宋武帝聞其美，召見奇之，曰：「真千里駒也。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Song heard of his excellence, summoned and marveled at him, saying: "Truly a thousand-li colt.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Song heard of him, summoned him, and marveled: "A true thousand-li colt.

sentences.zh: 」以為世子中軍參軍，數見接引。

translations.literal: " He was made middle army secretary to the heir apparent and was repeatedly received in audience.
translations.idiomatic: " He became middle army secretary to the heir and was often received in audience.

sentences.zh: 累遷江夏王義恭撫軍記室參軍。

translations.literal: He rose through appointments to recording secretary on the pacification staff of Prince Yigong of Jiangxia.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to recording secretary on the pacification staff of Prince Yigong of Jiangxia.

sentences.zh: 義恭就文帝求一學義沙門，會敷赴假還江陵，入辭，文帝令以後車載沙門往，謂曰：「道中可得言晤。

translations.literal: Yigong asked Emperor Wen for a monk learned in doctrine; as Fu was returning on leave to Jiangling to take leave, the Emperor had a monk sent in the rear carriage and told him: "On the road you may converse.
translations.idiomatic: Yigong asked Emperor Wen for a learned monk; as Fu was returning to Jiangling on leave, the emperor had a monk ride in the rear carriage and said, "You may talk doctrine on the road.

sentences.zh: 」敷不奉詔，曰：「臣性不耐雜。

translations.literal: " Fu did not obey the edict and said: "By nature I cannot endure clutter.
translations.idiomatic: " Fu refused the order: "By nature I cannot endure clutter.

sentences.zh: 」上甚不悅。

translations.literal: " The Emperor was very displeased.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor was deeply displeased.

sentences.zh: 遷正員中書郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to regular attendant of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to regular attendant of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 敷小名樝，父邵小名梨。

translations.literal: Fu's childhood name was Zha; his father Shao's childhood name was Li.
translations.idiomatic: Fu's childhood name was Zha; his father Shao's was Li.

sentences.zh: 文帝戲之曰：「樝何如梨？

translations.literal: Emperor Wen teased him: "How does Zha compare with Li?
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen teased him: "How does Zha compare with Li?

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「梨是百果之宗，樝何敢比也。

translations.literal: " He answered: "The pear is sovereign among fruits—how dare Zha compare with it?
translations.idiomatic: " He answered: "The pear is sovereign among fruits. How dare Zha compare?

sentences.zh: 」中書舍人秋當、周赳並管要務，以敷同省名家欲詣之。

translations.literal: The secretariat attendants Qiu Dang and Zhou Jiu both handled weighty affairs and, because Fu was a famous man of the same office, wished to call on him.
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat attendants Qiu Dang and Zhou Jiu handled weighty affairs and, because Fu was a famous colleague, wanted to call on him.

sentences.zh: 赳曰：「彼若不相容接，便不如勿往，詎可輕行。

translations.literal: Jiu said: "If he will not receive us properly, we had better not go—how can we go lightly?
translations.idiomatic: Jiu said, "If he won't receive us properly, we'd better not go. How can we visit so casually?

sentences.zh: 」當曰：「吾等並已員外郎矣，何憂不得共坐。

translations.literal: " Dang said: "We are already outer-office gentlemen—why worry that we cannot sit together?
translations.idiomatic: " Dang said, "We're already outer-office gentlemen. Why worry we can't sit together?

sentences.zh: 」敷先旁設二床，去壁三四尺。

translations.literal: Fu first set up two seats off to the side, three or four chi from the wall.
translations.idiomatic: Fu first placed two seats to one side, three or four chi from the wall.

sentences.zh: 二客就席，敷呼左右曰：「移我遠客。

translations.literal: When the two guests took their seats, Fu called to his attendants: "Move me farther from these distant guests.
translations.idiomatic: When the guests sat down, Fu called to his attendants: "Move me farther from these distant guests.

sentences.zh: 」赳等失色而去，其自標遇如此。

translations.literal: " Jiu and the others turned pale and left—such was the way he marked his standing.
translations.idiomatic: " Jiu and the others blanched and left. Such was the way he marked his standing.

sentences.zh: 善持音儀，盡詳緩之致，與人別，執手曰：「念相聞。

translations.literal: Skilled in maintaining tone and bearing, with every detail of grace and ease, when parting from others he would take their hands and say: "Think of keeping in touch.
translations.idiomatic: Master of tone and bearing, graceful in every detail, he would take people's hands at parting and say, "Think of keeping in touch.

sentences.zh: 」餘響久之不絕。

translations.literal: " The lingering sound long did not fade.
translations.idiomatic: " The lingering sound hung in the air.

sentences.zh: 張氏後進皆慕之，其源起自敷也。

translations.literal: The younger men of the Zhang clan all admired this; the fashion began with Fu.
translations.idiomatic: Younger Zhangs all imitated him; the fashion began with Fu.

sentences.zh: 遷黃門侍郎，始興王浚後將軍司徒左長史，未拜，父在吳興亡，成服凡十餘日，始進水漿。

translations.literal: Promoted to Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, then left chief secretary to Prince Jun of Shixing, rear general and left chief secretary to the minister of works—before taking up the post his father died in Wuxing; he wore mourning for more than ten days before he first took water or broth.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to gentleman of the yellow gate and slated for left chief secretary to Prince Jun of Shixing, rear general and minister of works, he had not yet taken up the post when his father died in Wuxing. He mourned more than ten days before drinking even water.

sentences.zh: 葬畢不進鹽菜，遂毀瘠成疾。

translations.literal: After the burial he took no salt or vegetables and wasted away into illness.
translations.idiomatic: After the burial he ate no salt or vegetables and wasted away into illness.

sentences.zh: 伯父茂度每止譬之，輒更感慟，絕而復續。

translations.literal: His uncle Maodu often came to comfort him, but each time Fu only grieved the more, fainting and reviving.
translations.idiomatic: His uncle Maodu often tried to comfort him, but each visit only deepened Fu's grief until he fainted and revived.

sentences.zh: 茂度曰：「我冀譬汝有益，但更甚耳。

translations.literal: Maodu said: "I hoped comforting you would help, but it only makes it worse.
translations.idiomatic: Maodu said, "I hoped comfort would help, but it only makes it worse.

sentences.zh: 」自是不復往。

translations.literal: " After that he no longer came.
translations.idiomatic: " After that he stopped coming.

sentences.zh: 未期而卒。

translations.literal: Before his term of mourning ended he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died before mourning ended.

sentences.zh: 孝武即位，詔旌其孝道，追贈侍中，改其所居稱孝張裏。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu took the throne he issued an edict honoring his filial piety, posthumously made him attendant-in-ordinary, and renamed his residence Filial Zhang Lane.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu took the throne he honored Fu's filial piety, posthumously made him attendant-in-ordinary, and renamed his lane Filial Zhang Lane.

sentences.zh: 敷弟柬襲父封，位通直郎。

translations.literal: Fu's younger brother Jian inherited their father's fief and served as direct gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Fu's brother Jian inherited the fief and served as direct gentleman.

sentences.zh: 柬勇力，手格猛獸，元凶以為輔國將軍。

translations.literal: Jian was strong and once grappled with a fierce beast bare-handed; the crown prince made him general who assists the state.
translations.idiomatic: Jian was strong enough to wrestle fierce beasts bare-handed; the crown prince made him general who assists the state.

sentences.zh: 孝武至新亭，柬出奔，墜淮死。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu reached Xinting, Jian fled and fell into the Huai and drowned.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu reached Xinting, Jian fled, fell into the Huai, and drowned.

sentences.zh: 子式嗣。

translations.literal: His son Shi succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shi succeeded.

sentences.zh: 弟沖。

translations.literal: Younger brother Chong.
translations.idiomatic: Younger brother Chong.

sentences.zh: 沖字思約，出繼伯父敷。

translations.literal: Chong, styled Siyue, was adopted to continue the line of his uncle Fu.
translations.idiomatic: Chong, styled Siyue, was adopted to continue his uncle Fu's line.

sentences.zh: 沖母戴顒女，有儀范，張氏內取則焉。

translations.literal: Chong's mother was a daughter of Dai Yong and had dignity and grace; within the Zhang household she was the standard.
translations.idiomatic: Chong's mother, a daughter of Dai Yong, had dignity and grace and set the standard within the Zhang household.

sentences.zh: 沖少有至性，隨從叔永為將帥，除盱眙太守。

translations.literal: Chong from youth had utmost filial nature; following his uncle Yong as a commander, he was appointed governor of Xuyi.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Chong showed deep filial feeling. Following his uncle Yong as a commander, he became governor of Xuyi.

sentences.zh: 永征彭城遇寒，軍人足脛凍斷者十七八，沖足指皆墮。

translations.literal: When Yong marched on Pengcheng in bitter cold, seventeen or eighteen out of ten soldiers had feet and shins frozen off; Chong lost all his toes.
translations.idiomatic: When Yong marched on Pengcheng in bitter cold, nearly eight in ten soldiers lost feet or shins to frostbite; Chong lost all his toes.

sentences.zh: 齊永明八年，為假節，監青冀二州行刺史事。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Yongming he held provisional credentials and supervised the acting governors of Qing and Ji provinces.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongming 8 he held provisional credentials and supervised acting governors of Qing and Ji provinces.

sentences.zh: 沖父初卒，遺命「祭我必以鄉土所產，無用牲物」。

translations.literal: When Chong's father first died he left instructions: "Sacrifice to me only with local produce of the homeland—do not use sacrificial animals."
translations.idiomatic: When Chong's father died he left instructions: "Sacrifice to me only with local produce from home—no sacrificial animals."

sentences.zh: 沖在鎮，四時還吳國取果菜，每至烝嘗，輒流涕薦焉。

translations.literal: While Chong was in his post, each season he sent back to Wu to fetch fruit and vegetables; at every seasonal offering he wept as he presented them.
translations.idiomatic: While in office he sent each season to Wu for fruit and vegetables and wept as he offered them at every seasonal rite.

sentences.zh: 仍轉刺史。

translations.literal: He was then transferred to full governor.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made full governor.

sentences.zh: 永元二年，為南兗州刺史，遷司州。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongyuan he was made governor of Southern Yan Province and transferred to Si Province.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongyuan 2 he became governor of Southern Yan Province, then moved to Si Province.

sentences.zh: 裴叔業以壽春降魏，又遷沖南兗州刺史，並未拜。

translations.literal: When Pei Shuye surrendered Shouyang to Wei, Chong was again transferred to governor of Southern Yan Province—neither appointment was taken up.
translations.idiomatic: When Pei Shuye surrendered Shouyang to Wei, Chong was again named governor of Southern Yan Province, but he never took either post.

sentences.zh: 崔慧景事平，征建安王寶夤還都，以沖為郢州刺史，一歲之中，頻授四州刺史，至是乃受任，封定襄侯。

translations.literal: After Cui Huijing's affair was settled, the court recalled Prince Bao of Jian'an to the capital and made Chong governor of Ying Province; within one year he was four times offered governorships of four provinces—only now did he accept, and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Dingxiang.
translations.idiomatic: After Cui Huijing's revolt was crushed, the court recalled Prince Bao of Jian'an and made Chong governor of Ying Province. Within a year he was offered four provincial governorships; only then did he accept, and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Dingxiang.

sentences.zh: 梁武帝起兵，手書喻意，又遣辯士說之，沖確然不回。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Liang raised troops he wrote personally to explain his intent and also sent eloquent envoys to persuade Chong, but Chong remained steadfast and would not turn.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Liang raised his banner he wrote personally and sent eloquent envoys to win Chong over, but Chong would not budge.

sentences.zh: 東昏遣驍騎將軍薛元嗣、制局監暨榮伯領兵及糧運送沖，使拒西師。

translations.literal: Emperor Donghun sent the fierce cavalry general Xue Yuansi and the control-bureau inspector Ji Rongbo to lead troops and grain transports to Chong, ordering him to resist the western army.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Donghun sent fierce cavalry general Xue Yuansi and control-bureau inspector Ji Rongbo with troops and grain to reinforce Chong and hold the western army at bay.

sentences.zh: 元嗣等懲劉山陽之敗，疑沖不敢進，停住夏首浦。

translations.literal: Yuansi and the others, chastened by Liu Shanyang's defeat, doubted Chong would advance and halted at Xiashou Ford.
translations.idiomatic: Yuansi and the others, chastened by Liu Shanyang's defeat, doubted Chong would advance and halted at Xiashou Ford.

sentences.zh: 聞梁武師將至，元嗣、榮伯相率入郢城。

translations.literal: Hearing that Liang Wu's army was approaching, Yuansi and Rongbo together entered Ying city.
translations.idiomatic: When they heard Liang Wu's army was near, Yuansi and Rongbo entered Ying city together.

sentences.zh: 時竟陵太守房僧寄被代還至郢，東昏敕僧寄留守魯山，除驍騎將軍。

translations.literal: At that time the acting governor of Jingling, Fang Sengji, replaced and returning to Ying, Emperor Donghun ordered Sengji to hold Lushan and made him fierce cavalry general.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Fang Sengji, acting governor of Jingling, was returning to Ying after being replaced. Donghun ordered him to hold Lushan and made him fierce cavalry general.

sentences.zh: 僧寄謂沖曰：「下官雖未荷朝廷深恩，實蒙先帝厚澤。

translations.literal: Sengji said to Chong: "Though I have not received deep grace from the court, I truly owe a heavy debt to the late emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Sengji told Chong, "I may not owe the court deep favor, but I owe the late emperor a heavy debt.

sentences.zh: 蔭其樹者不折其枝，實欲微立塵效。

translations.literal: One who enjoys the shade of a tree does not break its branches—I truly wish to render some small service.
translations.idiomatic: One who enjoys a tree's shade does not break its branches. I wish to render some small service.

sentences.zh: 」沖深相許諾，共結盟誓，分部拒守。

translations.literal: " Chong pledged himself deeply and they swore an alliance, dividing forces to hold their positions.
translations.idiomatic: " Chong pledged himself deeply. They swore an alliance and divided forces to hold their positions.

sentences.zh: 遣軍主孫樂祖數千人助僧寄據魯山岸立城壘。

translations.literal: He sent the army commander Sun Lezu with several thousand men to help Sengji hold the Lushan shore and build fortifications.
translations.idiomatic: He sent army commander Sun Lezu with several thousand men to help Sengji hold the Lushan shore and build fortifications.

sentences.zh: 明年二月，梁武圍魯山城，遣軍主曹景宗等過江攻郢城。

translations.literal: In the second month of the following year Liang Wu besieged Lushan city and sent army commanders Cao Jingzong and others across the river to attack Ying city.
translations.idiomatic: The next second month Liang Wu besieged Lushan and sent commanders like Cao Jingzong across the river to attack Ying city.

sentences.zh: 沖中兵參軍陳光靜等間出擊之，光靜戰死，沖固守不出。

translations.literal: Chong's middle army secretary Chen Guangjing and others slipped out to strike them; Guangjing died in battle and Chong held firm without coming out.
translations.idiomatic: Chong's secretary Chen Guangjing slipped out to attack them, died in battle, and Chong held firm without sallying forth.

sentences.zh: 病將死，厲府僚以誠節，言終而卒。

translations.literal: Ill and near death, he sternly charged his staff with loyalty and died as he finished speaking.
translations.idiomatic: Ill and near death, he sternly charged his staff to hold loyal and died as he finished speaking.

sentences.zh: 元嗣、榮伯與衝子孜及長史江夏程茂固守。

translations.literal: Yuansi, Rongbo, Chong's son Zi, and chief secretary Cheng Mao of Jiangxia held firm.
translations.idiomatic: Yuansi, Rongbo, Chong's son Zi, and chief secretary Cheng Mao of Jiangxia continued the defense.

sentences.zh: 東昏詔贈沖散騎常侍、護軍將軍。

translations.literal: Emperor Donghun issued an edict posthumously making Chong attendant-in-ordinary and general who protects the army.
translations.idiomatic: Donghun posthumously made Chong attendant-in-ordinary and general who protects the army.

sentences.zh: 元嗣等處圍城之中，無他經略，唯迎蔣子文及蘇侯神，日禺中於州聽上祀以求福，鈴鐸聲晝夜不止。

translations.literal: Yuansi and the others, trapped in the besieged city with no other strategy, only welcomed Jiang Ziwen and the spirit of Marquis Su, at midday in the provincial hall offering sacrifice for blessing, with bells and clappers day and night without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Trapped in the siege with no strategy, Yuansi and the others only welcomed Jiang Ziwen and the spirit of Marquis Su, offering sacrifice at noon in the provincial hall for blessing, bells and clappers ringing day and night.

sentences.zh: 又使子文導從登陴巡行，旦日輒復如之。

translations.literal: They also had Ziwen as guide ascend the walls on inspection; each dawn they did the same again.
translations.idiomatic: They also had Ziwen as guide patrol the walls; each dawn they did the same again.

sentences.zh: 識者知其將亡。

translations.literal: Those who understood saw that they were doomed.
translations.idiomatic: Those who understood knew they were doomed.

sentences.zh: 僧寄病死，孫樂祖窘，以城降。

translations.literal: Sengji died of illness; Sun Lezu, hard pressed, surrendered the city.
translations.idiomatic: Sengji died of illness. Hard pressed, Sun Lezu surrendered the city.

sentences.zh: 郢被圍二百餘日，士庶病死者七八百家。

translations.literal: Ying was besieged for more than two hundred days; among officials and commoners seven or eight hundred households died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Ying was besieged over two hundred days; seven or eight hundred households of officials and commoners died of sickness.

sentences.zh: 魯山陷後二日，程茂及元嗣等議降，使孜為書與梁武帝。

translations.literal: Two days after Lushan fell, Cheng Mao and Yuansi and the others debated surrender and had Zi write to Emperor Wu of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Two days after Lushan fell, Cheng Mao and Yuansi debated surrender and had Zi write to Emperor Wu of Liang.

sentences.zh: 沖故吏青州中從事房長瑜謂孜曰：「前使君忠貫昊天，操愈松竹，郎君但當端坐畫一，以荷析薪。

translations.literal: Chong's former clerk Fang Changyu of Qing Province, middle attendant, said to Zi: "The former governor's loyalty pierced heaven, his integrity surpassed pine and bamboo—you need only sit upright and draw one stroke to bear the burden of firewood.
translations.idiomatic: Chong's former clerk Fang Changyu told Zi, "Your father's loyalty pierced heaven and his integrity surpassed pine and bamboo. You need only sit upright and draw one line to bear the burden of firewood.

sentences.zh: 若天運不與，幅巾待命，以下從使君。

translations.literal: If Heaven's fortune is not with us, wrap your head in cloth and await fate, then follow your father below.
translations.idiomatic: If Heaven's fortune fails, wrap your head in cloth and await fate, then follow your father below.

sentences.zh: 今若隨諸人之計，非唯郢州士女失高山之望，亦恐彼所不取也。

translations.literal: If you now follow the others' plan, not only will the people of Ying lose their hope in a high mountain, I fear the enemy will not accept it either.
translations.idiomatic: If you follow the others now, not only will the people of Ying lose their pillar, I fear the enemy will not accept it either.

sentences.zh: 」不從，卒以郢城降。

translations.literal: " They did not listen and in the end surrendered Ying city.
translations.idiomatic: " They refused. Ying city surrendered.

sentences.zh: 時以沖及房僧寄比臧洪之被圍也。

translations.literal: At the time Chong and Fang Sengji were compared to Zang Hong under siege.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Chong and Fang Sengji were compared to Zang Hong under siege.

sentences.zh: 贈僧寄益州刺史。

translations.literal: Sengji was posthumously made governor of Yi Province.
translations.idiomatic: Sengji was posthumously made governor of Yi Province.

sentences.zh: 暢字少微，邵兄褘子也。

translations.literal: Chang, styled Shaowei, was the son of Shao's elder brother Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Chang, styled Shaowei, was the son of Shao's elder brother Hui.

sentences.zh: 褘少有操行，為晉琅邪王國郎中令。

translations.literal: Hui from youth had integrity and conduct and served as director of the bureau of the Prince of Langye's kingdom.
translations.idiomatic: Hui from youth had integrity and served as director of the bureau of the Prince of Langye's kingdom.

sentences.zh: 從王至洛。

translations.literal: He followed the prince to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the prince to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 還京都，宋武帝封藥酒一罌付褘，使密加酖毒，受命於道自飲而卒。

translations.literal: Returning to the capital, Emperor Wu of Song entrusted Hui with a jar of medicinal wine and ordered him to add poison in secret; on the road he received the charge and drank it himself and died.
translations.idiomatic: Returning to the capital, Liu Yu gave Hui a jar of medicinal wine and ordered him to add poison in secret. On the road he drank it himself and died.

sentences.zh: 暢少與從兄敷、演、鏡齊名，為後進之秀。

translations.literal: Chang from youth was famed with his cousins Fu, Yan, and Jing as the finest of the younger generation.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Chang was famed with cousins Fu, Yan, and Jing as the finest of the younger generation.

sentences.zh: 起家為太守徐佩之主簿，佩之被誅，暢馳出奔赴，制服盡哀，為論者所美。

translations.literal: He first entered service as chief clerk to Governor Xu Peizhi; when Peizhi was executed, Chang galloped out to attend him, wore mourning and grieved fully, and was praised by commentators.
translations.idiomatic: He first served as chief clerk to Governor Xu Peizhi. When Peizhi was executed, Chang galloped out to attend him, wore mourning, and grieved fully—commentators praised him.

sentences.zh: 弟牧嘗為猘犬所傷，醫雲宜食蝦蟆，牧甚難之。

translations.literal: His younger brother Mu was once bitten by a mad dog; the physician said he should eat toads, which Mu found very difficult.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Mu was bitten by a mad dog; the physician said he should eat toads, which Mu found unbearable.

sentences.zh: 暢含笑先嘗，牧因此乃食，創亦即愈。

translations.literal: Chang smiled and tasted first; Mu then ate and the wound healed.
translations.idiomatic: Chang smiled, tasted first, and Mu then ate and healed.

sentences.zh: 累遷太子中庶子。

translations.literal: He rose through appointments to junior mentor of the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to junior mentor of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 孝武鎮彭城，暢為安北長史、沛郡太守。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu was stationed at Pengcheng, Chang was chief secretary of the northern pacification army and governor of Pei Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu held Pengcheng, Chang was chief secretary of the northern pacification army and governor of Pei Commandery.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十七年，魏太武南征，太尉江夏王義恭統諸軍出鎮彭城。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year of Yuanjia the Wei Emperor Taiwu marched south; Grand Commandant Prince Yigong of Jiangxia commanded the armies and went out to hold Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanjia 27 the Wei emperor Taiwu marched south. Grand commandant Prince Yigong of Jiangxia took the field to hold Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 太武親率大眾，去彭城數十里。

translations.literal: Taiwu personally led the great host to within several tens of li of Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Taiwu personally led the great host to within several tens of li of Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 彭城眾力雖多，軍食不足，義恭欲棄彭城南歸，計議彌日不定。

translations.literal: Though Pengcheng's forces were many, military provisions were insufficient; Yigong wished to abandon Pengcheng and return south, and for a whole day deliberation did not settle.
translations.idiomatic: Though Pengcheng's forces were many, provisions ran short. Yigong wished to abandon Pengcheng and retreat south; deliberation lasted a whole day without decision.

sentences.zh: 時曆城眾少食多，安北中兵參軍沈慶之議欲以車營為函箱陣，精兵為外翼，奉二王及妃媛直趨曆城，分城兵配護軍將軍蕭思話留守。

translations.literal: At that time Licheng had many troops and little food; Shen Qingzhi, middle army secretary of the northern pacification army, proposed forming wagons into a box-formation, elite troops as outer wings, escorting the two princes and consorts straight to Licheng, and assigning garrison troops to General Who Protects the Army Xiao Sihua to hold the city.
translations.idiomatic: Licheng had many troops but little food. Shen Qingzhi, middle army secretary of the northern pacification army, proposed wagons in box formation, elite troops as outer wings, escorting the two princes and consorts straight to Licheng while garrison troops under General Xiao Sihua held the city.

sentences.zh: 太尉長史何勖不同，欲席捲奔鬱洲，自海道還都。

translations.literal: Grand Commandant chief secretary He Xu disagreed and wished to roll up and flee to Yuzhou, returning to the capital by sea.
translations.idiomatic: Chief secretary He Xu disagreed and wanted to flee wholesale to Yuzhou and return to court by sea.

sentences.zh: 二議未決，更集群僚謀之。

translations.literal: The two plans undecided, they again gathered the staff to deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: With both plans unsettled, they gathered the staff again.

sentences.zh: 暢曰：

translations.literal: Chang said:
translations.idiomatic: Chang said:

sentences.zh: 「若曆城、鬱洲有可至之理，下官敢不高贊。

translations.literal: "If Licheng and Yuzhou were reachable, your humble servant would not dare fail to approve highly.
translations.idiomatic: "If Licheng and Yuzhou were reachable, I would not fail to approve.

sentences.zh: 今城內乏食，百姓咸有走情，但以關扃嚴固，欲去莫從耳。

translations.literal: Now within the city provisions are scarce and the people all have the mind to flee, but because the gates and barriers are strict they wish to go yet cannot.
translations.idiomatic: But provisions inside are scarce and everyone wants to flee; only strict gates keep them from running.

sentences.zh: 若一旦動腳，則各自散走，欲至所在，何由可得？

translations.literal: If we stir once, each will scatter on his own—when we wish to reach our destination, how can we arrive?
translations.idiomatic: Stir once and each will scatter—how then can we reach anywhere?

sentences.zh: 今軍食雖寡，朝夕猶未窘罄，豈有舍萬安之術，而就危亡之道。

translations.literal: Though military grain is little, morning and evening we are not yet utterly exhausted—how can we abandon a ten-thousand-fold safe plan and take the road to peril and death?
translations.idiomatic: Our grain is thin but not yet gone. How can we abandon safety for ruin?

sentences.zh: 若此計必用，下官請以頸血汙君馬跡。

translations.literal: If this plan must be used, your humble servant asks to stain your horse's tracks with the blood of my neck.
translations.idiomatic: If you take that plan, I ask to stain your horse's tracks with my neck's blood.

sentences.zh: 」孝武聞暢議，謂義恭曰：「張長史言不可異也。

translations.literal: " Emperor Xiaowu heard Chang's counsel and said to Yigong: "Chief Secretary Zhang's words must not be changed.
translations.idiomatic: " Emperor Xiaowu heard Chang and told Yigong, "Chief Secretary Zhang's words must stand.

sentences.zh: 」義恭乃止。

translations.literal: " Yigong then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: " Yigong stopped.

sentences.zh: 魏太武得至，仍登城南亞父塚，于戲馬台立氈屋。

translations.literal: When the Wei Emperor Taiwu arrived he still climbed the southern city's mound of the foster father of Qi and set up a felt tent on the Play-Horses Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: When Taiwu arrived he climbed the southern mound of Qi's foster father and set up a felt tent on the Play-Horses Terrace.

sentences.zh: 先是隊主蒯應見執，其日晡時，太武遣送應至小巿門致意，求甘蔗及酒。

translations.literal: Earlier the squad leader Kuai Ying had been captured; that day in the hour of the ram Taiwu sent Ying to the small market gate with greetings, asking for sugarcane and wine.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier squad leader Kuai Ying had been captured. That afternoon Taiwu sent Ying to the small market gate with greetings, asking for sugarcane and wine.

sentences.zh: 孝武遣人送酒二器，甘蔗百挺；

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu sent two jars of wine and a hundred stalks of sugarcane;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu sent two jars of wine and a hundred stalks of sugarcane;

sentences.zh: 求駱駝。

translations.literal: they asked for camels.
translations.idiomatic: they asked for camels.

sentences.zh: 明日，太武又自上戲馬台，復遣使至小巿門求與孝武相見，遣送駱駝並致雜物，使于南門受之。

translations.literal: The next day Taiwu again ascended the Play-Horses Terrace and again sent envoys to the small market gate asking to meet Emperor Xiaowu, sending camels and various goods to be received at the south gate.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Taiwu again ascended the Play-Horses Terrace and sent envoys to the small market gate asking to meet Emperor Xiaowu, sending camels and goods to be received at the south gate.

sentences.zh: 暢于城上與魏尚書李孝伯語。

translations.literal: Chang on the wall spoke with Wei Minister of the Interior Li Xiaobo.
translations.idiomatic: Chang on the wall spoke with Wei minister Li Xiaobo.

sentences.zh: 孝伯問：「君何姓？

translations.literal: Xiaobo asked: "What is your surname?
translations.idiomatic: Xiaobo asked, "What is your surname?

sentences.zh: 」答云：「姓張。

translations.literal: " He answered: "The surname is Zhang.
translations.idiomatic: " He answered, "Zhang.

sentences.zh: 」孝伯曰：「張長史。

translations.literal: " Xiaobo said: "Chief Secretary Zhang.
translations.idiomatic: " Xiaobo said, "Chief Secretary Zhang.

sentences.zh: 」暢曰：「君何得見識？

translations.literal: " Chang said: "How do you recognize me?
translations.idiomatic: " Chang said, "How do you know me?

sentences.zh: 」孝伯曰：「君聲名遠聞，足使我知。

translations.literal: " Xiaobo said: "Your fame reaches far—enough to let me know.
translations.idiomatic: " Xiaobo said, "Your fame reaches far—that is enough to know you.

sentences.zh: 」因言說久之。

translations.literal: " They then spoke at length.
translations.idiomatic: " They then spoke at length.

sentences.zh: 城內有具思者嘗在魏，義恭遣視，知是孝伯，乃開門進餉物。

translations.literal: Within the city was Ju Si, who had once been in Wei; Yigong sent to look and knew it was Xiaobo, then opened the gate to send in provisions.
translations.idiomatic: Within the city was Ju Si, who had served in Wei. Yigong sent to look, recognized Xiaobo, and opened the gate to send provisions.

sentences.zh: 太武又求酒及甘橘，暢宣孝武旨，又致螺杯雜粽，南土所珍。

translations.literal: Taiwu again asked for wine and sweet oranges; Chang announced Emperor Xiaowu's intent and also sent spiral cups and assorted rice dumplings, treasures of the southern lands.
translations.idiomatic: Taiwu again asked for wine and sweet oranges. Chang announced Emperor Xiaowu's reply and sent spiral cups and assorted rice dumplings, southern delicacies.

sentences.zh: 太武復令孝伯傳語曰：「魏主有詔借博具。

translations.literal: Taiwu again had Xiaobo relay words: "The Wei lord has an edict to borrow gaming pieces.
translations.idiomatic: Taiwu again had Xiaobo relay: "The Wei lord has an edict to borrow gaming pieces.

sentences.zh: 」暢曰：「博具當為申致，有詔之言，政可施于彼國，何得稱之於此。

translations.literal: " Chang said: "Gaming pieces I shall convey; but the words 'has an edict'—that may be applied to their country—how can it be spoken here?
translations.idiomatic: " Chang said, "Gaming pieces I will send. But 'has an edict' applies to their country—how can it be spoken here?

sentences.zh: 」孝伯曰：「鄰國之君，何為不稱詔於鄰國之臣？

translations.literal: " Xiaobo said: "The lord of a neighboring state—why may he not speak of an edict to a minister of a neighboring state?
translations.idiomatic: " Xiaobo said, "Why may a neighboring lord not speak of an edict to a neighboring minister?

sentences.zh: 」暢曰：「君之此稱，尚不可聞于中華，況在諸王之貴，而獨曰鄰國之君邪。

translations.literal: " Chang said: "This way of speaking of yours should not be heard even in the Central Lands—much less among princes of the highest rank; can one alone say 'lord of a neighboring state'?
translations.idiomatic: " Chang said, "That way of speaking should not be heard even in the Central Lands—much less among princes. Can one simply say 'neighboring lord'?

sentences.zh: 」孝伯曰：「魏主言太尉、鎮軍久闕南信，殊當憂邑，若欲遣信，當為護送。

translations.literal: " Xiaobo said: "The Wei lord says the Grand Commandant and the Pacification General have long lacked news from the south and are deeply troubled; if you wish to send messages, he will escort them.
translations.idiomatic: " Xiaobo said, "The Wei lord says the grand commandant and pacification general have long lacked news from the south and are deeply troubled. If you wish to send messages, he will escort them.

sentences.zh: 」暢曰：「此方間路甚多，不復以此勞魏主。

translations.literal: " Chang said: "This region has many side routes—we need not trouble the Wei lord with this.
translations.idiomatic: " Chang said, "This region has many routes. We need not trouble the Wei lord.

sentences.zh: 」孝伯曰：「亦知有水路，似為白賊所斷。

translations.literal: " Xiaobo said: "We also know there is a water route, but it seems cut by white bandits.
translations.idiomatic: " Xiaobo said, "We know there is a water route too, but white bandits seem to have cut it.

sentences.zh: 」暢曰：「君著白衣，故稱白賊邪？

translations.literal: " Chang said: "You wear white robes—so you call them white bandits?
translations.idiomatic: " Chang said, "You wear white robes—so you call them white bandits?

sentences.zh: 」孝伯大笑曰：「今之白賊亦不異黃巾、赤眉。

translations.literal: " Xiaobo laughed loudly: "Today's white bandits are no different from the Yellow Turbans and Red Eyebrows.
translations.idiomatic: " Xiaobo laughed: "Today's white bandits are no different from the Yellow Turbans and Red Eyebrows.

sentences.zh: 」暢曰：「黃巾、赤眉似不在江南。

translations.literal: " Chang said: "Yellow Turbans and Red Eyebrows seem not to be in the lands south of the Yangtze.
translations.idiomatic: " Chang said, "Yellow Turbans and Red Eyebrows are not south of the Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 」孝伯曰：「亦不離青、徐。

translations.literal: " Xiaobo said: "They are also not far from Qing and Xu.
translations.idiomatic: " Xiaobo said, "Nor are they far from Qing and Xu.

sentences.zh: 」暢曰：「今者青、徐實為有賊，但非白賊耳。

translations.literal: " Chang said: "Today Qing and Xu truly have bandits—but they are not white bandits.
translations.idiomatic: " Chang said, "Qing and Xu do have bandits today—but not white ones.

sentences.zh: 」又求博具，俄送與。

translations.literal: " They again asked for gaming pieces and soon they were sent.
translations.idiomatic: " They asked again for gaming pieces and soon received them.

sentences.zh: 太武又遣送氈及九種鹽並胡豉，云：「此諸鹽各有所宜：白鹽是魏主所食；

translations.literal: Taiwu again sent felt rugs and nine kinds of salt plus fermented bean paste, saying: "Each of these salts has its use: white salt is what the Wei lord eats;
translations.idiomatic: Taiwu again sent felt rugs, nine kinds of salt, and fermented bean paste, saying: "Each salt has its use: white salt is what the Wei lord eats;

sentences.zh: 黑者療腹脹氣懣，細刮取六銖，以酒服之；

translations.literal: black cures abdominal swelling and choking—scrape six zhu fine and take with wine;
translations.idiomatic: black cures abdominal swelling—scrape six zhu fine and take with wine;

sentences.zh: 胡鹽療目痛；

translations.literal: Hu salt cures eye pain;
translations.idiomatic: Hu salt cures eye pain;

sentences.zh: 柔鹽不用食，療馬脊創；

translations.literal: soft salt is not for eating—it treats wounds on a horse's spine;
translations.idiomatic: soft salt is not for eating—it treats wounds on a horse's spine;

sentences.zh: 赤鹽、駁鹽、臭鹽、馬齒鹽四種，並不中食。

translations.literal: red salt, mottled salt, stinking salt, and horse-tooth salt—four kinds—are all unfit for food.
translations.idiomatic: red, mottled, stinking, and horse-tooth salt—four kinds—are unfit for food.

sentences.zh: 胡豉亦中噉。

translations.literal: The fermented bean paste is also good to eat.
translations.idiomatic: The fermented bean paste is also good to eat.

sentences.zh: 」又求黃甘，並云：「魏主致意太尉、安北，何不遣人來至我間？

translations.literal: " They again asked for yellow sweet oranges and also said: "The Wei lord sends greetings to the Grand Commandant and the Northern Pacification General—why not send someone to visit us?
translations.idiomatic: " They asked for yellow sweet oranges and said: "The Wei lord greets the grand commandant and northern pacification general. Why not send someone to visit us?

sentences.zh: 彼此之情雖不可盡，要須見我小大，知我老少，觀我為人。

translations.literal: Though feelings between us cannot be fully expressed, you must at least see our young and old, know our ages, and observe what manner of men we are.
translations.idiomatic: Feelings between us cannot be fully told, but you should at least see our young and old, know our ages, and observe what manner of men we are.

sentences.zh: 若諸佐不可遣，亦可使僮來。

translations.literal: If your aides cannot be sent, servants may come.
translations.idiomatic: If your aides cannot come, send servants.

sentences.zh: 」暢又宣旨答曰：「魏主形狀才力，久為來往所具，李尚書親自銜命，不患彼此不盡。

translations.literal: " Chang again announced the reply: "The Wei lord's form, talent, and strength have long been known through mutual exchanges; Minister Li personally bears the charge—there is no fear feelings will not be fully expressed.
translations.idiomatic: " Chang replied: "The Wei lord's form and strength have long been known through exchanges. Minister Li bears the charge in person—feelings will be fully expressed.

sentences.zh: 故不復遣信。

translations.literal: Therefore we send no messenger again.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore we send no messenger again.

sentences.zh: 」又云：「魏主恨向所送馬殊不稱意，安北若須大馬，當更送之；

translations.literal: " They also said: "The Wei lord regrets the horses sent earlier were quite unsatisfactory; if the Northern Pacification General needs large horses, more may be sent;
translations.idiomatic: " They also said: "The Wei lord regrets the horses sent earlier were unsatisfactory. If the northern pacification general needs large horses, more may be sent;

sentences.zh: 脫須蜀馬，亦有佳者。

translations.literal: if Shu horses are needed, fine ones are also available.
translations.idiomatic: if Shu horses are needed, fine ones are available too.

sentences.zh: 」暢曰：「安北不乏良駟，送自彼意，非此所求。

translations.literal: " Chang said: "The Northern Pacification General lacks no fine steeds—the gift came from their side, not from a request here.
translations.idiomatic: " Chang said, "The northern pacification general lacks no fine steeds. The gift came from their side, not from a request here.

sentences.zh: 」義恭又餉炬燭十挺，孝武亦致錦一匹。

translations.literal: Yigong also sent ten bundles of torch-candles; Emperor Xiaowu also sent a bolt of brocade.
translations.idiomatic: Yigong also sent ten bundles of torch candles; Emperor Xiaowu sent a bolt of brocade.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「知更須黃甘，誠非所吝，但會不足周彼一軍。

translations.literal: They also said: "Knowing you further need yellow sweet oranges—we are truly not stingy, but the season cannot supply their whole army.
translations.idiomatic: They also said, "Knowing you need yellow sweet oranges—we are not stingy, but the season cannot supply their whole army.

sentences.zh: 向給魏主，未應便乏，故不復重付。」

translations.literal: What was given the Wei lord earlier should not yet be exhausted—therefore we do not send again."
translations.idiomatic: What we gave the Wei lord earlier should not be exhausted—therefore we do not send again."

sentences.zh: 太武復求甘蔗安石榴，暢曰：「石榴出自鄴下，亦當非彼所乏。

translations.literal: Taiwu again asked for sugarcane and pomegranates; Chang said: "Pomegranates come from below Ye—surely they are not lacking there either.
translations.idiomatic: Taiwu again asked for sugarcane and pomegranates. Chang said, "Pomegranates come from below Ye—they cannot be lacking there either.

sentences.zh: 」孝伯曰：「君南土膏粱，何為著屩？

translations.literal: " Xiaobo said: "You, a fine grain of the southern lands—why wear straw sandals?
translations.idiomatic: " Xiaobo said, "You, a fine grain of the south—why wear straw sandals?

sentences.zh: 君而著此，使將士雲何？

translations.literal: You wearing these—what are your officers and soldiers to do?
translations.idiomatic: You wearing these—what are your officers and soldiers to do?

sentences.zh: 」暢曰：「膏粱之言，誠為多愧，但以不武，受命統軍，戎陣之間，不容緩服。」

translations.literal: " Chang said: "The words 'fine grain' are truly much to blush at—but being unwarlike and charged to command the army, between battle lines one cannot wear loose robes."
translations.idiomatic: " Chang said, "Fine grain' is much to blush at—but unwarlike as I am, charged to command between battle lines, one cannot wear loose robes."

sentences.zh: 太武又遣就二王借箜篌、琵琶、箏、笛等器及棋子。

translations.literal: Taiwu again sent to borrow from the two princes the konghou, pipa, zither, flute, and other instruments plus chess pieces.
translations.idiomatic: Taiwu again sent to borrow from the two princes the konghou, pipa, zither, flute, and other instruments plus chess pieces.

sentences.zh: 孝伯辭辯亦北土之美，暢隨宜應答，吐屬如流，音韻詳雅，風儀華潤。

translations.literal: Xiaobo's eloquence was also a northern beauty; Chang answered as occasion required with flowing words, tone refined and bearing luminous.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaobo's eloquence was a northern marvel too; Chang answered as occasion required with flowing words, refined tone, and luminous bearing.

sentences.zh: 孝伯及左右人並相視歎息。

translations.literal: Xiaobo and those beside him all looked at one another and sighed.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaobo and those beside him looked at one another and sighed.

sentences.zh: 時魏聲雲當出襄陽，故以暢為南譙王義宣司空長史、南郡太守。

translations.literal: At that time Wei voices said they would move on Xiangyang, so Chang was made chief secretary to Prince Yixuan of Southern Qiao, minister of works, and governor of Nan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei voices said they would move on Xiangyang, Chang was made chief secretary to Prince Yixuan of Southern Qiao, minister of works, and governor of Nan Commandery.

sentences.zh: 三十年，元凶弑逆，義宣發哀之日，即便舉兵。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year the crown prince committed regicide; on the day Yixuan raised mourning he at once raised troops.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year the crown prince committed regicide. The day Yixuan began mourning he raised troops.

sentences.zh: 暢為元佐，位居僚首，哀容俯仰，蔭映當時。

translations.literal: Chang as chief aide held the foremost rank among staff; in mourning bearing, bowing and rising, he cast a shadow over the moment.
translations.idiomatic: Chang as chief aide ranked first among staff; in mourning bearing, bowing and rising, he cast a shadow over the moment.

sentences.zh: 舉哀畢，改服著黃褲褶，出射堂簡人。

translations.literal: When mourning was finished he changed dress to yellow trousers and jacket and went to the archery hall to select men.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he changed to yellow trousers and jacket and went to the archery hall to select men.

sentences.zh: 音姿容止，莫不矚目，見者皆願為盡命。

translations.literal: In voice, bearing, and deportment none failed to fix their eyes; those who saw him all wished to give their lives.
translations.idiomatic: Voice, bearing, and deportment fixed every eye; those who saw him wished to give their lives.

sentences.zh: 事平，徵為吏部尚書，封夷道縣侯。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled he was summoned as minister of personnel and enfeoffed as Marquis of Yidao.
translations.idiomatic: When the affair was settled he was summoned as minister of personnel and enfeoffed as Marquis of Yidao.

sentences.zh: 義宣既有異圖，蔡超等以暢人望，勸義宣留之。

translations.literal: Yixuan already harbored a separate design; Cai Chao and others, because of Chang's public standing, urged Yixuan to keep him.
translations.idiomatic: Yixuan already harbored separate designs. Cai Chao and others, because of Chang's standing, urged Yixuan to keep him.

sentences.zh: 乃解南蠻校尉以授暢，加冠軍將軍，領丞相長史。

translations.literal: They then removed the colonel of the southern barbarians and gave it to Chang, added general who champions the army, and put him in charge of the chief minister's staff.
translations.idiomatic: They removed the colonel of the southern barbarians and gave it to Chang, added general who champions the army, and put him in charge of the chief minister's staff.

sentences.zh: 暢遣門生荀僧寶下都，因顏竣陳義宣釁狀。

translations.literal: Chang sent his student Xun Sengbao down to the capital to report Yixuan's signs of rebellion through Yan Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Chang sent his student Xun Sengbao to the capital to report Yixuan's rebellion through Yan Jun.

sentences.zh: 僧寶有私貨，停巴陵不時下。

translations.literal: Sengbao had private goods and halted at Baling without coming down in time.
translations.idiomatic: Sengbao had private goods and halted at Baling without coming down in time.

sentences.zh: 會義宣起兵，津路斷絕，僧寶遂不得去。

translations.literal: Just as Yixuan raised troops the ferry routes were cut and Sengbao could not leave.
translations.idiomatic: Just as Yixuan raised troops the ferry routes were cut and Sengbao could not leave.

sentences.zh: 義宣將為逆，遣嬖人翟靈寶告暢，暢陳必無此理，請以死保之。

translations.literal: As Yixuan was about to rebel he sent his favorite Zhai Lingbao to tell Chang; Chang declared there could be no such reason and asked to guarantee it with his life.
translations.idiomatic: As Yixuan was about to rebel he sent favorite Zhai Lingbao to tell Chang. Chang declared it impossible and asked to guarantee it with his life.

sentences.zh: 靈寶知暢不回，勸義宣殺以徇眾，賴丞相司馬竺超人得免。

translations.literal: Lingbao knew Chang would not turn and urged Yixuan to kill him to show the masses; thanks to chief minister's marshal Zhu Chaoren he escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Lingbao knew Chang would not turn and urged Yixuan to kill him to rally the masses. Thanks to chief minister's marshal Zhu Chaoren he escaped.

sentences.zh: 進號撫軍，別立軍部，以收人望。

translations.literal: He was promoted to pacification general and a separate army headquarters was set up to gather public esteem.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to pacification general and a separate army headquarters was set up to gather public esteem.

sentences.zh: 暢雖署文檄，而飲酒常醉，不省文書。

translations.literal: Though Chang signed proclamations, he drank constantly drunk and did not examine documents.
translations.idiomatic: Though Chang signed proclamations, he drank constantly and ignored documents.

sentences.zh: 隨義宣東下。

translations.literal: He followed Yixuan east.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Yixuan east.

sentences.zh: 梁山戰敗，於亂兵自歸，為軍人所掠，衣服都盡。

translations.literal: When Liangshan was defeated he returned of his own accord in the rout and was stripped by soldiers until his clothes were entirely gone.
translations.idiomatic: When Liangshan fell he returned in the rout and soldiers stripped him bare.

sentences.zh: 遇右將軍王玄謨乘輿出營，暢已得敗衣，因排玄謨上輿。

translations.literal: He met Right General Wang Xuanmo riding out in a carriage; Chang had already found cast-off clothes and pushed Xuanmo up into the carriage.
translations.idiomatic: He met Right General Wang Xuanmo riding out in a carriage. Chang had found cast-off clothes and pushed Xuanmo into the carriage.

sentences.zh: 玄謨意甚不悅，諸將請殺之，隊主張世營救得免。

translations.literal: Xuanmo was very displeased; the generals asked to kill him but squad leader Zhang Shiying rescued him and he escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanmo was deeply displeased. Generals asked to kill him but squad leader Zhang Shiying rescued him.

sentences.zh: 執送都，下廷尉，尋見原。

translations.literal: Seized and sent to the capital, sent to the minister of justice, he was soon pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Seized and sent to court, tried by the minister of justice, he was soon pardoned.

sentences.zh: 起為都官尚書，轉侍中，代子淹領太子右衛率。

translations.literal: He was raised as minister of justice, transferred to attendant-in-ordinary, and replaced his son Yan as leader of the heir's right guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was raised as minister of justice, transferred to attendant-in-ordinary, and replaced his son Yan as leader of the heir's right guard.

sentences.zh: 孝武宴朝賢，暢亦在坐。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu feasted the court worthies and Chang was also among them.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu feasted court worthies and Chang was among them.

sentences.zh: 何偃因醉曰：「張暢故是奇才，同義宣作賊，亦能無咎，非才何以致此？

translations.literal: He Yan, drunk, said: "Zhang Chang is truly a rare talent—even joining Yixuan in rebellion he escaped blame; if not talent, how reach this?
translations.idiomatic: He Yan, drunk, said, "Zhang Chang is truly rare—even joining Yixuan in rebellion he escaped blame. Without talent how reach this?

sentences.zh: 」暢乃厲聲曰：「太初之時，誰黃其合？

translations.literal: " Chang sternly cried: "In the Taichu era, who yellowed the toilet?
translations.idiomatic: " Chang cried sternly, "In the Taichu era, who yellowed the toilet?

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「何事相苦。

translations.literal: " The Emperor said: "Why torment each other.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "Why torment each other.

sentences.zh: 」初，元凶時，偃父尚之為元凶司空，義師至新林，門生皆逃，尚之父子與婢妾共洗黃合，故暢譏之。

translations.literal: " At first during the crown prince's time Yan's father Shangzhi had been the crown prince's minister of works; when the righteous army reached Xinlin the students all fled—Shangzhi father and son with maidservants together scrubbed the yellow toilet, hence Chang's mockery.
translations.idiomatic: " During the crown prince's time Yan's father Shangzhi had been his minister of works. When the righteous army reached Xinlin the students all fled—Shangzhi father and son scrubbed the yellow toilet with maidservants, hence Chang's mockery.

sentences.zh: 孝建二年，出為會稽太守。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xiaojian he went out as governor of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: In Xiaojian 2 he went out as governor of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡曰宣。

translations.literal: He died and was given the posthumous name Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was given the posthumous name Xuan.

sentences.zh: 暢愛弟子輯，臨終遺命，與輯合墳，論者非之。

translations.literal: Chang loved his student Ji; on his deathbed he left orders to be buried in one tomb with Ji—commentators criticized this.
translations.idiomatic: Chang loved his student Ji. On his deathbed he ordered burial in one tomb with Ji—commentators criticized this.

sentences.zh: 暢弟悅亦有美稱，曆侍中、臨海王子頊前軍長史、南郡太守。

translations.literal: Chang's younger brother Yue also had a fine reputation and served as attendant-in-ordinary, chief secretary to Prince Zixiang of Linhai, front army, and governor of Nan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Chang's brother Yue also had a fine reputation and served as attendant-in-ordinary, chief secretary to Prince Zixiang of Linhai, and governor of Nan Commandery.

sentences.zh: 晉安王子勳建偽號，召拜為吏部尚書，與鄧琬共輔偽政。

translations.literal: When Prince Zixun of Jin'an set up a false reign he was summoned and made minister of personnel, jointly assisting the false government with Deng Wan.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Zixun of Jin'an set up a false reign he was summoned as minister of personnel and jointly assisted the false government with Deng Wan.

sentences.zh: 事敗，悅殺琬歸降，復為太子中庶子。

translations.literal: When the affair failed Yue killed Wan and surrendered; he again became junior mentor of the heir.
translations.idiomatic: When the affair failed Yue killed Wan and surrendered. He again became junior mentor of the heir.

sentences.zh: 後拜雍州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he was made governor of Yong Province.
translations.idiomatic: Later he became governor of Yong Province.

sentences.zh: 泰始六年，明帝于巴郡置三巴校尉，以悅補之，加持節、輔師將軍，領巴郡太守。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Taishi Emperor Ming set up the colonel of the Three Ba in Ba Commandery and appointed Yue to it, adding credential staff, general who assists the army, and concurrent governor of Ba Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In Taishi 6 Emperor Ming set up the colonel of the Three Ba in Ba Commandery and appointed Yue, adding credential staff, general who assists the army, and concurrent governor of Ba Commandery.

sentences.zh: 未拜卒。

translations.literal: He died before taking up the post.
translations.idiomatic: He died before taking up the post.

sentences.zh: 暢子浩，官至義陽王昶征北諮議參軍。

translations.literal: Chang's son Hao rose to advisory secretary on Prince Chang of Yiyang's northern pacification staff.
translations.idiomatic: Chang's son Hao rose to advisory secretary on Prince Chang of Yiyang's northern pacification staff.

sentences.zh: 浩弟淹，黃門郎，封廣晉縣子，太子右衛率，東陽太守。

translations.literal: Hao's younger brother Yan was gentleman of the yellow gate, enfeoffed as Viscount of Guangjin, leader of the heir's right guard, and governor of Dongyang.
translations.idiomatic: Hao's brother Yan was gentleman of the yellow gate, enfeoffed as Viscount of Guangjin, leader of the heir's right guard, and governor of Dongyang.

sentences.zh: 逼郡吏燒臂照佛。

translations.literal: He forced district clerks to burn their arms as lamp-offerings to the Buddha.
translations.idiomatic: He forced district clerks to burn their arms as lamp-offerings to the Buddha.

sentences.zh: 百姓有罪，使禮佛贖愆，動至數千拜。

translations.literal: When commoners had offenses he made them worship the Buddha to atone, often to several thousand prostrations.
translations.idiomatic: When commoners offended he made them worship the Buddha to atone, often to thousands of prostrations.

sentences.zh: 坐免官禁錮。

translations.literal: He was dismissed and confined.
translations.idiomatic: He was dismissed and confined.

sentences.zh: 起為光祿勳，臨川內史。

translations.literal: He was raised as superintendent of the imperial household and interior administrator.
translations.idiomatic: He was raised as superintendent of the imperial household and interior administrator.

sentences.zh: 後與晉安王子勳同逆，軍敗見殺。

translations.literal: Later he joined Prince Zixun of Jin'an in rebellion; defeated in battle he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Later he joined Prince Zixun of Jin'an in rebellion and was killed in defeat.

sentences.zh: 淹弟融。

translations.literal: Yan's younger brother Rong.
translations.idiomatic: Yan's younger brother Rong.

sentences.zh: 浮海至交州，于海中遇風，終無懼色，方詠曰：「幹魚自可還其本鄉，肉脯復何為者哉。

translations.literal: He crossed the sea to Jiaozhou; on the sea he met wind and showed no fear, reciting: "Dried fish may naturally return to their native streams—what need for jerky?
translations.idiomatic: He crossed the sea to Jiaozhou. Caught in wind at sea he showed no fear and recited: "Dried fish may return to their native streams—what need for jerky?

sentences.zh: 」又作海賦，文辭詭激，獨與眾異。

translations.literal: " He also wrote an Ode to the Sea, its language strange and sharp, alone unlike others.
translations.idiomatic: " He also wrote an Ode to the Sea, strange and sharp, unlike anyone else.

sentences.zh: 後以示鎮軍將軍顧覬之，覬之曰：「卿此賦實超玄虛，但恨不道鹽耳。

translations.literal: Later he showed it to General Who Pacifies the Army Gu Kaizhi; Kaizhi said: "Your fu truly surpasses the abstruse void—but I regret it does not mention salt.
translations.idiomatic: He showed it to General Gu Kaizhi. Kaizhi said, "Your fu surpasses the abstruse void—but I regret it does not mention salt.

sentences.zh: 」融即求筆注曰：「漉沙構白，熬波出素，積雪中春，飛霜暑路。

translations.literal: " Rong at once asked for a brush and added: "Filtering sand builds white; boiling waves yields pure; snow piled in mid-spring; frost flying on a summer road.
translations.idiomatic: " Rong asked for a brush and added: "Filtering sand builds white; boiling waves yields pure; snow piled in mid-spring; frost flying on a summer road.

sentences.zh: 」此四句後所足也。

translations.literal: " These four lines were added afterward.
translations.idiomatic: " These four lines were added afterward.

sentences.zh: 覬之與融兄有恩好，覬之卒，融身負墳土。

translations.literal: Kaizhi and Rong's elder brother had friendly ties; when Kaizhi died Rong personally carried earth for the tomb.
translations.idiomatic: Kaizhi and Rong's elder brother were friends. When Kaizhi died Rong personally carried earth for the tomb.

sentences.zh: 在南與交趾太守卞展善。

translations.literal: In the south he was on good terms with Jiaozhi Governor Bian Zhan.
translations.idiomatic: In the south he was close to Jiaozhi Governor Bian Zhan.

sentences.zh: 展於嶺南為人所殺，融挺身奔赴。

translations.literal: Zhan was killed by men in Lingnan; Rong rushed to attend in person.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan was killed in Lingnan. Rong rushed to attend in person.

sentences.zh: 舉秀才，對策中第。

translations.literal: He was recommended as outstanding talent and ranked first in the palace examination.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended as outstanding talent, he ranked first in the palace examination.

sentences.zh: 為尚書殿中郎，不就，改為儀曹郎。

translations.literal: He was made director in the Secretariat but did not take the post and was changed to director in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Made director in the secretariat he did not take the post and was changed to director in the ministry of rites.

sentences.zh: 尋請假奔叔父喪，道中罰幹錢敬道鞭杖五十，寄系延陵獄。

translations.literal: Soon he asked leave to rush to his uncle's funeral; on the road he had his servant Gan Jingdao flogged fifty strokes and sent to be held in Yanchuan prison.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he asked leave to rush to his uncle's funeral. On the road he had servant Gan Jingdao flogged fifty strokes and sent to Yanchuan prison.

sentences.zh: 大明五年制，二品清官行僮幹杖，不得出十。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Daming regulations, for second-rank pure offices the rod for errant servants could not exceed ten strokes.
translations.idiomatic: In Daming 5 regulations for second-rank pure offices limited rods for errant servants to ten strokes.

sentences.zh: 為左丞孫緬所奏，免官。

translations.literal: Left assistant Sun Mian memorialized against him and he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Left assistant Sun Mian memorialized against him and he was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 重定，攝祠部、倉部二曹。

translations.literal: Reappointed, he acted in the ministries of sacrifices and granaries.
translations.idiomatic: Reappointed, he acted in the ministries of sacrifices and granaries.

sentences.zh: 時領軍劉勉戰死，融以祠部議，上應哭勉，見從。

translations.literal: At that time the army leader Liu Mian died in battle; Rong on the sacrifices ministry's deliberation argued the court should mourn Mian and was followed.
translations.idiomatic: When army leader Liu Mian died in battle, Rong on the sacrifices ministry argued the court should mourn Mian and was followed.

sentences.zh: 又俗人忌以正月開太倉，融議不宜拘束小忌。

translations.literal: Again common people tabooed opening the great granary in the first month; Rong argued small taboos should not bind.
translations.idiomatic: Commoners tabooed opening the great granary in the first month; Rong argued small taboos should not bind.

sentences.zh: 尋兼掌正廚，見宰殺，回車徑去，自表解職。

translations.literal: Soon he also oversaw the imperial kitchen; seeing slaughter he turned his carriage and left, memorializing himself to resign.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he also oversaw the imperial kitchen. Seeing slaughter he turned his carriage and left and memorialized to resign.

sentences.zh: 再遷南陽王友。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to friend of the Prince of Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was again transferred to friend of the Prince of Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 融父暢為丞相長史，義宣事難，暢將為王玄謨所殺，時玄謨子瞻為南陽王長史，融啟求去官，不許。

translations.literal: Rong's father Chang had been chief minister's secretary; when Yixuan's affair was in crisis Chang was about to be killed by Wang Xuanmo; at that time Xuanmo's son Zhan was chief secretary to the Prince of Nanyang—Rong memorialized asking to leave office and was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Rong's father Chang had been chief minister's secretary. When Yixuan's affair was in crisis Chang was about to be killed by Wang Xuanmo. Xuanmo's son Zhan was then chief secretary to the Prince of Nanyang—Rong memorialized to leave office and was refused.

sentences.zh: 融家貧欲祿，乃與從叔征北將軍永書曰：「融昔幼學，早訓家風，雖則不敏，率以成性。

translations.literal: Rong's family was poor and wanted salary; he wrote to his cousin Northern Pacification General Yong: "Rong from youth studied, early trained in the family style; though not clever, I have largely formed my nature.
translations.idiomatic: Rong's family was poor and wanted salary. He wrote his cousin Northern Pacification General Yong: "From youth I studied, early trained in family style. Though not clever, I have largely formed my nature.

sentences.zh: 布衣韋帶，弱年所安，簞食瓢飲，不覺不樂。
