translations.literal: Cloth coat and leather belt were what my weak years rested in; simple food and gourd drink—I felt no lack of joy.
translations.idiomatic: Cloth coat and leather belt were what my weak years rested in. Simple food and gourd drink—I felt no lack of joy.

sentences.zh: 但世業清貧，人生多待，榛栗棗修，女贄既長，束帛禽鳥，男禮已大。

translations.literal: But the family's occupation is pure poverty and life has many demands—hazelnuts, dates, and dried meat for daughters' dowries grown long, silk and birds for sons' rites already great.
translations.idiomatic: But the family's occupation is pure poverty and life has many demands—hazelnuts and dates for daughters' dowries, silk and birds for sons' rites.

sentences.zh: 勉身就官，十年七仕，不欲代耕，何至此事。

translations.literal: I forced myself into office—ten years, seven posts—not wishing to substitute for farming, how reach this?
translations.idiomatic: I forced myself into office—ten years, seven posts—not wishing to farm, how reach this?

sentences.zh: 昔求三吳一丞，雖屬舛錯，今聞南康缺守，願得為之。

translations.literal: Once I sought a Three Wu assistant post—though it went wrong; now I hear the Nankang governorship is vacant and wish to have it.
translations.idiomatic: Once I sought a Three Wu assistant post—though it went wrong. Now I hear Nankang is vacant and wish to have it.

sentences.zh: 融不知階級，階級亦可不知融，政以求丞不得，所以求郡，求郡不得，亦可復求丞。

translations.literal: Rong does not know ranks—ranks may also not know Rong; precisely because seeking assistant failed I seek commandery; seeking commandery failing, I may again seek assistant.
translations.idiomatic: Rong does not know ranks—ranks may not know Rong either. Because assistant failed I seek commandery; commandery failing, I may seek assistant again.

sentences.zh: 」又與吏部尚書王僧虔書曰：「融天地之逸人也，進不辨貴，退不知賤，實以家貧累積，孤寡傷心，八侄俱孤，二弟頓弱，豈能山海陋祿，申融情累。

translations.literal: " He also wrote to Minister of Personnel Wang Sengqian: "Rong is a recluse of heaven and earth—advancing he does not know the noble, retreating he does not know the base; truly family poverty accumulates, orphans and widows wound the heart—eight nephews all orphaned, two brothers weak—how can mountain-and-sea meager salary express Rong's emotional burdens.
translations.idiomatic: " He also wrote Minister of Personnel Wang Sengqian: "Rong is heaven and earth's recluse—advancing he does not know rank, retreating he does not know base. Family poverty accumulates, orphans and widows wound the heart—eight nephews orphaned, two brothers weak—how can meager salary express my burdens?

sentences.zh: 阮籍愛東平土風，融亦欣晉平閑外。

translations.literal: Ruan Ji loved the soil of Dongping—Rong also delights in Jinping beyond the passes.
translations.idiomatic: Ruan Ji loved Dongping's soil—Rong also delights in Jinping beyond the passes.

sentences.zh: 」時議以融非御人才，竟不果。

translations.literal: " At the time critics said Rong was no talent for governing—indeed it did not happen.
translations.idiomatic: " Critics said Rong was no governing talent—it did not happen.

sentences.zh: 辟齊太傅掾，稍遷中書郎，非其所好。

translations.literal: He was recruited as staff to the grand tutor of Qi and gradually rose to attendant of the Secretariat—not to his liking.
translations.idiomatic: Recruited as staff to the grand tutor of Qi he rose to attendant of the secretariat—not to his liking.

sentences.zh: 乞為中散大夫，不許。

translations.literal: He begged to be grand master of the palace and was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: He begged to be grand master of the palace and was refused.

sentences.zh: 張氏自敷以來，並以理音辭、修儀範為事。

translations.literal: From Fu onward the Zhang clan all made regulating tone and language and cultivating bearing their business.
translations.idiomatic: From Fu onward the Zhangs all made regulating tone and cultivating bearing their business.

sentences.zh: 至融風止詭越，坐常危膝，行則曳步，翹身仰首，意制甚多。

translations.literal: With Rong, bearing turned strange and surpassing—sitting he often perched on his knees, walking he dragged his steps, body lifted and head thrown back, with many deliberate gestures.
translations.idiomatic: With Rong bearing turned strange—sitting he perched on his knees, walking he dragged his steps, body lifted and head thrown back, with many deliberate gestures.

sentences.zh: 見者驚異，聚觀成巿，而融了無慚色。

translations.literal: Those who saw him were startled and gathered to watch until the street became a market—and Rong showed not a trace of shame.
translations.idiomatic: Onlookers were startled and crowds filled the street—and Rong showed not a trace of shame.

sentences.zh: 隨例同行，常稽遲不進。

translations.literal: Following custom in procession he often lagged and did not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Following custom in procession he often lagged and did not advance.

sentences.zh: 高帝素愛融，為太尉時，與融款接。

translations.literal: Emperor Gao of Qi had long loved Rong; when grand commandant he treated Rong warmly.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gao of Qi had long loved Rong. As grand commandant he treated Rong warmly.

sentences.zh: 見融常笑曰：「此人不可無一，不可有二。

translations.literal: Seeing Rong he would often laugh: "This man cannot be without one, cannot be two.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing Rong he would laugh: "This man cannot be without one, cannot be two.

sentences.zh: 」即位後，手詔賜融衣曰：「見卿衣服粗故，誠乃素懷有本。

translations.literal: " After taking the throne he personally wrote an edict gifting Rong clothes: "Seeing your clothes worn and plain, truly your plain heart has roots.
translations.idiomatic: " After taking the throne he wrote gifting Rong clothes: "Seeing your clothes worn and plain, truly your plain heart has roots.

sentences.zh: 交爾藍縷，亦虧朝望。

translations.literal: Yet giving you blue rags also diminishes the court's face.
translations.idiomatic: Yet giving you blue rags also diminishes the court's face.

sentences.zh: 今送一通故衣，意謂雖故，乃勝新也。

translations.literal: Now I send one set of old clothes—I mean though old it still surpasses new.
translations.idiomatic: Now I send one set of old clothes—though old it still surpasses new.

sentences.zh: 是吾所著，已令裁減，稱卿之體；

translations.literal: These I wore myself and have had cut to fit your frame;
translations.idiomatic: These I wore myself and had cut to fit your frame;

sentences.zh: 並履一量。

translations.literal: also one measure of shoes.
translations.idiomatic: also one measure of shoes.

sentences.zh: 」高帝出太極殿西室，融入問訊，彌時方登階。

translations.literal: " Emperor Gao left the west chamber of the Hall of Supreme Pole; Rong entered to pay respects and was long before mounting the steps.
translations.idiomatic: " Emperor Gao left the west chamber of the Hall of Supreme Pole. Rong entered to pay respects and was long before mounting the steps.

sentences.zh: 及就席，上曰：「何乃遲為？

translations.literal: When he took his seat the Emperor said: "Why so slow?
translations.idiomatic: When he took his seat the emperor said, "Why so slow?

sentences.zh: 「對曰：「自地升天，理不得速。

translations.literal: " He answered: "From earth ascending to heaven—by principle one cannot be fast.
translations.idiomatic: " He answered, "From earth ascending to heaven—by principle one cannot be fast.

sentences.zh: 」時魏主至淮而退，帝問：「何意忽來忽去。

translations.literal: " At that time the Wei lord reached the Huai and withdrew; the Emperor asked: "What meant coming and going so suddenly?
translations.idiomatic: " When the Wei lord reached the Huai and withdrew the emperor asked, "What meant coming and going so suddenly?

sentences.zh: 」未有答者，融時下坐，抗聲曰：「以無道而來，見有道而去。

translations.literal: " No one answered; Rong then rose from his lower seat and cried aloud: "He came without the Way and left upon seeing the Way.
translations.idiomatic: " No one answered. Rong rose from his lower seat and cried: "He came without the Way and left upon seeing the Way.

sentences.zh: 」公卿咸以為捷。

translations.literal: " The ministers all thought it sharp.
translations.idiomatic: " The ministers all thought it sharp.

sentences.zh: 融善草書，常自美其能。

translations.literal: Rong was skilled in cursive script and often praised his own ability.
translations.idiomatic: Rong was skilled in cursive script and often praised his own ability.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「卿書殊有骨力，但恨無二王法。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Your writing truly has bone-strength—but I regret it lacks the method of the Two Wangs.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Your writing truly has bone-strength—but I regret it lacks the Two Wangs' method.

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「非恨臣無二王法，亦恨二王無臣法。

translations.literal: " He answered: "It is not that I regret lacking the Two Wangs' method—it is also that the Two Wangs regret lacking my method.
translations.idiomatic: " He answered, "It is not that I regret lacking the Two Wangs' method—the Two Wangs regret lacking mine.

sentences.zh: 」融假還鄉，詣王儉別。

translations.literal: Rong took leave to return home and went to bid Wang Jian farewell.
translations.idiomatic: Rong took leave to return home and went to bid Wang Jian farewell.

sentences.zh: 儉立此地舉袂不前，融亦舉手呼儉曰：「歜曰'王前'。

translations.literal: Jian stood in this place and raised his sleeve without advancing; Rong also raised his hand and called to Jian: "Yu says 'Wang, forward'.
translations.idiomatic: Jian stood in place and raised his sleeve without advancing. Rong raised his hand and called, "Yu says 'Wang, forward'.

sentences.zh: 」儉不得已趨就之。

translations.literal: " Jian had no choice but to hurry to him.
translations.idiomatic: " Jian had no choice but to hurry to him.

sentences.zh: 融曰：「使融不為慕勢，而令君為趍士，豈不善乎。

translations.literal: Rong said: "If Rong did not crave influence and made you rush like a sycophant—is that not better?
translations.idiomatic: Rong said, "If I did not crave influence and made you rush like a sycophant—is that not better?

sentences.zh: 」常歎云：「不恨我不見古人，所恨古人又不見我。」

translations.literal: " He often sighed: "I do not regret that I never saw the ancients—I regret that the ancients never saw me."
translations.idiomatic: " He often sighed, "I do not regret never seeing the ancients—I regret the ancients never saw me."

sentences.zh: 融與吏部尚書何戢善，往詣戢，誤通尚書劉澄。

translations.literal: Rong was on good terms with Minister of Personnel He Ji and went to call on Ji but mistakenly entered to Minister of the Interior Liu Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: Rong was close to Minister of Personnel He Ji and went to call on Ji but mistakenly entered Minister of the Interior Liu Cheng's.

sentences.zh: 下車入門，乃曰：「非是。

translations.literal: Descending from the carriage and entering the gate he said: "Not this one.
translations.idiomatic: Descending from the carriage and entering the gate he said, "Not this one.

sentences.zh: 」至戶望澄，又曰：「非是。

translations.literal: " Reaching the door and seeing Cheng he again said: "Not this one.
translations.idiomatic: " Reaching the door and seeing Cheng he again said, "Not this one.

sentences.zh: 」既造席視澄曰：「都自非是。

translations.literal: " When he reached the mat and looked at Cheng he said: "Altogether not this one.
translations.idiomatic: " When he reached the mat and looked at Cheng he said, "Altogether not this one.

sentences.zh: 」乃去。

translations.literal: " Then he left.
translations.idiomatic: " Then he left.

sentences.zh: 其為異如此。

translations.literal: Such was his strangeness.
translations.idiomatic: Such was his strangeness.

sentences.zh: 又為長沙王鎮軍，竟陵王征北諮議，並領記室，司徒從事中郎。

translations.literal: He also served as pacification general for the Prince of Changsha, advisory secretary on the northern expedition staff of the Prince of Jingling, both concurrently recording secretary, and staff secretary to the minister of works.
translations.idiomatic: He also served as pacification general for the Prince of Changsha, advisory secretary on Prince Jingling's northern expedition staff, both concurrently recording secretary, and staff secretary to the minister of works.

sentences.zh: 永明二年，總明觀講，敕朝臣集聽。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongming lectures were held at the Zongming Observatory and the court was ordered to assemble and listen.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongming 2 lectures were held at the Zongming Observatory and the court was ordered to assemble and listen.

sentences.zh: 融扶入就榻，私索酒飲之。

translations.literal: Rong, supported in, took his couch and privately asked for wine and drank.
translations.idiomatic: Rong, supported in, took his couch and privately asked for wine and drank.

sentences.zh: 事畢，乃長歎曰：「嗚呼！

translations.literal: When it was over he sighed long: "Alas!
translations.idiomatic: When it was over he sighed long, "Alas!

sentences.zh: 仲尼獨何人哉。

translations.literal: Confucius—what sort of man was he?
translations.idiomatic: Confucius—what sort of man was he?

sentences.zh: 」為御史中丞到撝所奏免官，尋復職。

translations.literal: " Censor-in-chief Dao Hui memorialized against him and he was dismissed, soon reinstated.
translations.idiomatic: " Censor-in-chief Dao Hui memorialized against him and he was dismissed, soon reinstated.

sentences.zh: 融形貌短醜，精神清澈，王敬則見融革帶寬，殆將至髀，謂曰：「革帶太急。

translations.literal: Rong was short and ugly in form but clear in spirit; Wang Jingze seeing Rong's leather belt wide, nearly reaching his thighs, said: "The leather belt is too tight.
translations.idiomatic: Rong was short and ugly in form but clear in spirit. Wang Jingze seeing Rong's leather belt wide, nearly reaching his thighs, said, "The leather belt is too tight.

sentences.zh: 」融曰：「既非步吏，急帶何為？

translations.literal: " Rong said: "Since I am no foot-runner, why tighten the belt?
translations.idiomatic: " Rong said, "Since I am no foot-runner, why tighten the belt?

sentences.zh: 」融假東出，武帝問融住在何處，答曰：「臣陸處無屋，舟居無水。

translations.literal: " Rong took leave to go east; Emperor Wu asked where Rong lived and he answered: "Your servant on land has no house, on water has no boat.
translations.idiomatic: " Rong took leave to go east. Emperor Wu asked where Rong lived and he answered, "On land I have no house, on water I have no boat.

sentences.zh: 」後上問其從兄緒，緒曰：「融近東出，未有居止，權牽小船於岸上住。

translations.literal: " Later the Emperor asked his cousin Xu, who said: "Rong recently went east and has no fixed dwelling—he temporarily moors a small boat on the shore.
translations.idiomatic: " Later the emperor asked his cousin Xu, who said, "Rong recently went east with no fixed dwelling—he temporarily moors a small boat on shore.

sentences.zh: 」上大笑。

translations.literal: " The Emperor laughed loudly.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor laughed loudly.

sentences.zh: 後使融接對北使李道固，就席，道固顧而言曰：「張融是宋彭城長史張暢子不？

translations.literal: Later he had Rong receive the northern envoy Li Daogu; when they took their seats Daogu looked and said: "Is Zhang Rong the son of Zhang Chang, chief secretary of Pengcheng in Song?
translations.idiomatic: Later he had Rong receive northern envoy Li Daogu. When they took their seats Daogu looked and said, "Is Zhang Rong the son of Zhang Chang, chief secretary of Pengcheng in Song?

sentences.zh: 」融嚬蹙久之，曰：「先君不幸，名達六夷。

translations.literal: " Rong frowned long and said: "My late father, alas, made his name known to the six barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: " Rong frowned long and said, "My late father, alas, made his name known to the six barbarians.

sentences.zh: 」豫章王大會賓僚，融食炙，始行畢，行炙人便去。

translations.literal: At a great gathering of guests for the Prince of Yuzhang, Rong was eating roast meat; when the first round ended the server of roast left.
translations.idiomatic: At a great gathering for the Prince of Yuzhang, Rong was eating roast meat. When the first round ended the server left.

sentences.zh: 融欲求鹽蒜，口終不言，方搖食指，半日乃息。

translations.literal: Rong wanted salt and garlic but would not speak; he only wagged his forefinger and only after half a day did he stop.
translations.idiomatic: Rong wanted salt and garlic but would not speak. He only wagged his forefinger and only after half a day stopped.

sentences.zh: 出入朝廷，皆拭目驚觀之。

translations.literal: Entering and leaving the court all wiped their eyes and watched in astonishment.
translations.idiomatic: Entering and leaving court all wiped their eyes and watched in astonishment.

sentences.zh: 八年，朝臣賀眾瑞公事，融扶入拜起，復為有司所奏，見原。

translations.literal: In the eighth year court worthies congratulated on auspicious omens; Rong, supported in, bowed and rose and was again memorialized against by the relevant office and pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year court worthies congratulated on auspicious omens. Rong, supported in, bowed and rose and was again memorialized against and pardoned.

sentences.zh: 遷司徒兼右長史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to concurrent right chief secretary to the minister of works.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to concurrent right chief secretary to the minister of works.

sentences.zh: 竟陵張欣時為諸暨令，坐罪當死，欣時父興世討宋南譙王義宣，官軍欲殺融父暢，興世以袍覆暢而坐之，以此得免。

translations.literal: Zhang Xixin of Jingling was then magistrate of Zhuji and sentenced to death for crime; Xixin's father Xingshi had campaigned against Prince Yixuan of Southern Qiao in Song—the army wished to kill Rong's father Chang and Xingshi covered Chang with his robe and sat on him, thus saving him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xixin of Jingling was magistrate of Zhuji and sentenced to death. Xixin's father Xingshi had campaigned against Prince Yixuan of Southern Qiao in Song—the army wished to kill Rong's father Chang and Xingshi covered Chang with his robe and sat on him, saving him.

sentences.zh: 興世卒，融著高履為負土成墳。

translations.literal: When Xingshi died Rong wore high shoes and personally carried earth to form the tomb.
translations.idiomatic: When Xingshi died Rong wore high shoes and personally carried earth to form the tomb.

sentences.zh: 至是，融啟竟陵王子良乞代欣時死。

translations.literal: At this time Rong memorialized Prince Ziliang of Jingling begging to die in Xixin's place.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Rong memorialized Prince Ziliang of Jingling begging to die in Xixin's place.

sentences.zh: 子良答曰：「此乃是長史美事，恐朝有常典，不得如長史所懷。

translations.literal: Ziliang answered: "This is truly the chief secretary's fine act—but I fear the court has fixed statutes and cannot be as the chief secretary wishes.
translations.idiomatic: Ziliang answered, "This is truly the chief secretary's fine act—but I fear the court has fixed statutes and cannot be as you wish.

sentences.zh: 」遷黃門郎，太子中庶子，司徒左長史。

translations.literal: " He was transferred to gentleman of the yellow gate, junior mentor of the heir, and left chief secretary to the minister of works.
translations.idiomatic: " He was transferred to gentleman of the yellow gate, junior mentor of the heir, and left chief secretary to the minister of works.

sentences.zh: 融有孝義，忌月三旬不聽樂，事嫂甚謹。

translations.literal: Rong had filial righteousness; during the taboo month for thirty days he listened to no music and served his sister-in-law with utmost care.
translations.idiomatic: Rong had filial righteousness. During the taboo month for thirty days he listened to no music and served his sister-in-law with utmost care.

sentences.zh: 父暢臨終謂諸子曰：「昔丞相事難，吾以不同將見殺，緣司馬竺超人得活，爾等必報其子。

translations.literal: When his father Chang was dying he told his sons: "In the former chief minister's crisis I was about to be killed for dissenting—thanks to chief minister's marshal Zhu Chaoren I lived; you must repay his son.
translations.idiomatic: When his father Chang was dying he told his sons, "In the chief minister's crisis I was about to be killed for dissenting—thanks to marshal Zhu Chaoren I lived. You must repay his son.

sentences.zh: 」後超人孫微冬月遭母喪居貧，融吊之，悉脫衣以為賻，披牛被而反。

translations.literal: Later Chaoren's grandson Wei in winter suffered his mother's mourning and lived in poverty; Rong visited in condolence and stripped off all his clothes as funeral gifts, returning wrapped in an ox hide.
translations.idiomatic: Later Chaoren's grandson Wei mourned his mother in winter in poverty. Rong visited in condolence, stripped off all his clothes as funeral gifts, and returned wrapped in an ox hide.

sentences.zh: 常以兄事微。

translations.literal: He always treated Wei as an elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: He always treated Wei as an elder brother.

sentences.zh: 豫章王嶷、竟陵王子良薨，自以身經佐吏，哭輒盡慟。

translations.literal: When Prince Liao of Yuzhang and Prince Ziliang of Jingling died, since he himself had been their staff officer he wept with full grief at each mourning.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Liao of Yuzhang and Prince Ziliang of Jingling died, since he had been their staff officer he wept with full grief at each mourning.

sentences.zh: 建武四年，病卒，遺令建白旐無旒，不設祭，令人捉麈尾登屋復魂。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jianwu he died of illness; his last orders were to set up a white banner without tassels, no sacrifices, and have a man with a fly-whisk ascend the roof to summon the soul.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianwu 4 he died of illness. His last orders were a white banner without tassels, no sacrifices, and a man with a fly-whisk ascending the roof to summon the soul.

sentences.zh: 曰：「吾生平所善，自當陵雲一笑。

translations.literal: He said: "What I favored in life should naturally laugh above the clouds.
translations.idiomatic: He said, "What I favored in life should naturally laugh above the clouds.

sentences.zh: 三千買棺，無制新衾。

translations.literal: Three thousand to buy a coffin—do not order new quilts.
translations.idiomatic: Three thousand to buy a coffin—do not order new quilts.

sentences.zh: 左手執孝經、老子，右手執小品法華經。

translations.literal: Left hand holding the Classic of Filial Piety and Laozi, right hand holding the Xiaopin Lotus Sutra.
translations.idiomatic: Left hand holding the Classic of Filial Piety and Laozi, right hand holding the Xiaopin Lotus Sutra.

sentences.zh: 妾二人哀事畢，各遣還家。

translations.literal: The two concubines, when mourning rites are finished, each send home.
translations.idiomatic: The two concubines, when mourning rites are finished, each send home.

sentences.zh: 」曰：「吾生平之風調，何至使婦人行哭失聲，不須暫停閨合。」

translations.literal: " He said: "The bearing of my life—how reach the point of making women walk and weep aloud; no need to pause at the inner quarters."
translations.idiomatic: " He said, "The bearing of my life—how reach making women walk and weep aloud. No need to pause at the inner quarters."

sentences.zh: 融玄義無師法，而神解過人，高談鮮能抗拒。

translations.literal: Rong's Dark Learning had no teacher's method but his spiritual understanding surpassed others; in lofty discourse few could resist him.
translations.idiomatic: Rong's Dark Learning had no teacher's method but his spiritual understanding surpassed others. In lofty discourse few could resist him.

sentences.zh: 永明中遇疾，為門律，自序云：「吾文章之體，多為世人所驚，汝可師耳以心，不可使耳為心師也。

translations.literal: In Yongming when ill he made literary rules and in self-preface wrote: "The form of my writing is often what the world marvels at—you may take it as teacher with the heart; you must not make the ear the heart's teacher.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongming when ill he made literary rules and wrote in self-preface: "The form of my writing is often what the world marvels at—you may take it as teacher with the heart. Do not make the ear the heart's teacher.

sentences.zh: 夫文豈有常體，但以有體為常，政當有其體。

translations.literal: Writing surely has no fixed form—but to have form as constant is precisely to have that form.
translations.idiomatic: Writing has no fixed form—but to have form as constant is precisely to have that form.

sentences.zh: 丈夫當刪詩、書，制禮樂，何至因循寄人籬下。

translations.literal: A true man should delete the Odes and Documents, make rites and music—why to the end follow and lodge under another's eaves?
translations.idiomatic: A true man should delete the Odes and Documents and make rites and music—why follow and lodge under another's eaves?

sentences.zh: 」臨卒，又戒其子曰：「手澤存焉，父書不讀，況父音情，婉在其韻。

translations.literal: " Near death he again admonished his sons: "The touch of the hand remains—if a father's writing is unread, how much more a father's tone and feeling, graceful in its cadence.
translations.idiomatic: " Near death he again admonished his sons, "The touch of the hand remains—if a father's writing is unread, how much more tone and feeling graceful in cadence?

sentences.zh: 吾意不然，別遺爾旨。

translations.literal: My intent is not so—I leave you a separate intent.
translations.idiomatic: My intent is not so—I leave you a separate intent.

sentences.zh: 吾文體英變，變而屢奇，豈吾天挺，蓋不隤家聲。

translations.literal: My literary form is heroic and changing, changing again and again into marvels—is it my heaven-endowed nature? Surely it does not fall from the family voice.
translations.idiomatic: My literary form is heroic and changing, changing again into marvels—is it my heaven-endowed nature? Surely it does not fall from the family voice.

sentences.zh: 汝可號哭而看之。

translations.literal: You may wail and look at it.
translations.idiomatic: You may wail and look at it.

sentences.zh: 」融文集數十卷行於世，自名其集為玉海。

translations.literal: " Rong's collected works of several tens of rolls circulated in the world; he himself named the collection Jade Sea.
translations.idiomatic: " Rong's collected works of several tens of rolls circulated. He himself named the collection Jade Sea.

sentences.zh: 司徒褚彥回問其故，融云：「蓋玉以比德，海崇上善耳。

translations.literal: Minister of Works Chu Yanhui asked the reason; Rong said: "Jade compares to virtue, sea exalts the highest good.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works Chu Yanhui asked the reason. Rong said, "Jade compares to virtue, sea exalts the highest good.

sentences.zh: 」張氏前有敷、演、鏡、暢，後有充、融、卷、稷。

translations.literal: " Before the Zhang clan had Fu, Yan, Jing, and Chang; after came Chong, Rong, Juan, and Ji.
translations.idiomatic: " Earlier the Zhangs had Fu, Yan, Jing, and Chang; later came Chong, Rong, Juan, and Ji.

sentences.zh: 第六弟寶積，建武中，出為廬陵太守。

translations.literal: The sixth younger brother Baoji, in Jianwu, went out as governor of Luling.
translations.idiomatic: The sixth brother Baoji, in Jianwu, went out as governor of Luling.

sentences.zh: 時名流謝伷、何點、陸惠曉、孔珪至融弟鐵之舍。

translations.literal: At that time leading figures Xie You, He Dian, Lu Huixiao, and Kong Gui came to Rong's younger brother Tie's house.
translations.idiomatic: At that time leading figures Xie You, He Dian, Lu Huixiao, and Kong Gui came to Rong's brother Tie's house.

sentences.zh: 點造坐便曰：「今日可謂盛集，二五我兄弟之流，阿六張氏保家之子。

translations.literal: Dian upon taking his seat at once said: "Today may truly be called a grand gathering—two-fives are we brothers' sort, A-six is Zhang's house-preserving son.
translations.idiomatic: Dian upon taking his seat said, "Today may truly be called a grand gathering—two-fives are we brothers' sort, A-six is Zhang's house-preserving son.

sentences.zh: 」顧見王思遠曰：「卿詐作善，非實得也。

translations.literal: " Looking at Wang Siyuan he said: "You pretend to be good—not truly attained.
translations.idiomatic: " Looking at Wang Siyuan he said, "You pretend to be good—not truly attained.

sentences.zh: 」二五謂孔珪及融並第五。

translations.literal: " Two-fives meant Kong Gui and Rong were both fifth-born.
translations.idiomatic: " Two-fives meant Kong Gui and Rong were both fifth-born.

sentences.zh: 寶積永元中為湘州行事蕭穎胄於江陵，乘腰輿詣穎胄，舉動自若。

translations.literal: In Yongyuan Baoji was acting for Xiang Province under Xiao Yingzhou at Jiangling; riding a waist carriage he went to Yingzhou, bearing and movement entirely at ease.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongyuan Baoji was acting for Xiang Province under Xiao Yingzhou at Jiangling. Riding a waist carriage he went to Yingzhou, bearing and movement entirely at ease.

sentences.zh: 穎胄問：「何至之晚？

translations.literal: Yingzhou asked: "Why arrive so late?
translations.idiomatic: Yingzhou asked, "Why arrive so late?

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「本朝危亂，四海橫流，既不能為比干之死，實未忍為微子之去，是以至晚。

translations.literal: " He answered: "The dynasty is in peril and chaos, the four seas in flood—I could not be Bi Gan in death and truly could not bear to be Weizi in departure; therefore I came late.
translations.idiomatic: " He answered, "The dynasty is in peril, the four seas in flood—I could not die like Bi Gan and truly could not bear to leave like Weizi. Therefore I came late.

sentences.zh: 」穎胄深以為善，即用為相府諮議。

translations.literal: " Yingzhou deeply approved and at once made him advisory secretary to the chief minister's headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: " Yingzhou deeply approved and at once made him advisory secretary to the chief minister's headquarters.

sentences.zh: 後位御史中丞。

translations.literal: Later he served as censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: Later he served as censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 融與東海徐文伯兄弟厚。

translations.literal: Rong and the Xu brothers Wenbo of Donghai were close.
translations.idiomatic: Rong and the Xu brothers Wenbo of Donghai were close.

sentences.zh: 文伯字德秀，濮陽太守熙曾孫也。

translations.literal: Wenbo, styled Dexiu, was great-grandson of Governor Xi of Puyang.
translations.idiomatic: Wenbo, styled Dexiu, was great-grandson of Governor Xi of Puyang.

sentences.zh: 熙好黃、老，隱于秦望山，有道士過求飲，留一瓠盧瓜與之，曰：「君子孫宜以道術救世，當得二千石。

translations.literal: Xi loved Huang-Lao and hid on Mount Qinwang; a Daoist passing asked to drink, left a gourd-bottle melon and said: "Your descendants should use the Way to save the age—you will obtain the two-thousand-shi rank.
translations.idiomatic: Xi loved Huang-Lao and hid on Mount Qinwang. A Daoist passing asked to drink, left a gourd-bottle melon and said, "Your descendants should use the Way to save the age—you will obtain the two-thousand-shi rank.

sentences.zh: 」熙開之，乃扁鵲鏡經一卷，因精心學之，遂名震海內。

translations.literal: " Xi opened it—it was one roll of Bian Que's Mirror Classic; he studied it with full heart and his name shook the land within the seas.
translations.idiomatic: " Xi opened it—it was one roll of Bian Que's Mirror Classic. He studied it with full heart and his name shook the land within the seas.

sentences.zh: 生子秋夫，彌工其術，仕至射陽令。

translations.literal: He begot Qiufu, who mastered the art even more and rose to magistrate of Sheyang.
translations.idiomatic: He begot Qiufu, who mastered the art even more and rose to magistrate of Sheyang.

sentences.zh: 嘗夜有鬼呻吟，聲甚悽愴，秋夫問何須，答言姓某，家在東陽，患腰痛死。

translations.literal: Once at night a ghost groaned, the sound very mournful; Qiufu asked what was needed and it answered surnamed so-and-so, family in Dongyang, died of back pain.
translations.idiomatic: Once at night a ghost groaned, the sound very mournful. Qiufu asked what was needed and it answered surnamed so-and-so, family in Dongyang, died of back pain.

sentences.zh: 雖為鬼痛猶難忍，請療之。

translations.literal: Though a ghost the pain was still hard to bear—please treat it.
translations.idiomatic: Though a ghost the pain was still hard to bear—please treat it.

sentences.zh: 秋夫曰：「雲何厝法？

translations.literal: Qiufu said: "How to set the method?
translations.idiomatic: Qiufu said, "How to set the method?

sentences.zh: 」鬼請為芻人，案孔穴針之，秋夫如言，為灸四處，又針肩井三處，設祭埋之。

translations.literal: " The ghost asked to be made a straw man; pressing the acupoints he needled it—Qiufu did as told, moxaed four places and needled three at shoulder-well, set out offerings and buried it.
translations.idiomatic: " The ghost asked to be made a straw man. Pressing the acupoints he needled it—Qiufu did as told, moxaed four places and needled three at shoulder-well, set out offerings and buried it.

sentences.zh: 明日見一人謝恩，忽然不見。

translations.literal: The next day a man came to give thanks and suddenly vanished.
translations.idiomatic: The next day a man came to give thanks and suddenly vanished.

sentences.zh: 當世伏其通靈。

translations.literal: The age submitted to his spirit-link.
translations.idiomatic: The age submitted to his spirit-link.

sentences.zh: 秋夫生道度、叔向，皆能精其業。

translations.literal: Qiufu begot Daodu and Shuxiang, both able to refine the craft.
translations.idiomatic: Qiufu begot Daodu and Shuxiang, both able to refine the craft.

sentences.zh: 道度有腳疾不能行，宋文帝令乘小輿入殿，為諸皇子療疾，無不絕驗。

translations.literal: Daodu had foot ailment and could not walk; Emperor Wen of Song had him carried in a small palanquin into the hall to treat the princes' illnesses—all without fail.
translations.idiomatic: Daodu had foot ailment and could not walk. Emperor Wen of Song had him carried in a small palanquin into the hall to treat the princes' illnesses—all without fail.

sentences.zh: 位蘭陵太守。

translations.literal: He served as governor of Lanling.
translations.idiomatic: He served as governor of Lanling.

sentences.zh: 宋文帝云：「天下有五絕，而皆出錢唐。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Song said: "Under heaven there are five supreme arts—and all come from Qiantang.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Song said, "Under heaven there are five supreme arts—and all come from Qiantang.

sentences.zh: 」謂杜道鞠彈棋，範悅詩，褚欣遠模書，褚胤圍棋，徐道度療疾也。

translations.literal: " He meant Du Daoju's ball-game, Fan Yue's poetry, Chu Xinyuan's chess-calligraphy, Chu Yin's go, and Xu Daodu's healing.
translations.idiomatic: " He meant Du Daoju's ball-game, Fan Yue's poetry, Chu Xinyuan's chess-calligraphy, Chu Yin's go, and Xu Daodu's healing.

sentences.zh: 道度生文伯，叔向生嗣伯。

translations.literal: Daodu begot Wenbo; Shuxiang begot Sibo.
translations.idiomatic: Daodu begot Wenbo; Shuxiang begot Sibo.

sentences.zh: 文伯亦精其業，兼有學行，倜儻不屈意於公卿，不以醫自業。

translations.literal: Wenbo also refined the craft and had learning and conduct, free and unbowed before dukes and ministers—not making medicine his profession.
translations.idiomatic: Wenbo also refined the craft and had learning and conduct, free and unbowed before dukes and ministers—not making medicine his profession.

sentences.zh: 融謂文伯、嗣伯曰：「昔王微、嵇叔夜並學而不能，殷仲堪之徒故所不論。

translations.literal: Rong told Wenbo and Sibo: "In the past Wang Wei and Ji Kang both studied yet could not succeed—the likes of Yin Zhongkan are therefore not discussed.
translations.idiomatic: Rong told Wenbo and Sibo, "Wang Wei and Ji Kang both studied yet could not succeed—the likes of Yin Zhongkan are therefore not discussed.

sentences.zh: 得之者由神明洞徹，然後可至，故非吾徒所及。

translations.literal: Attaining it comes from spirit penetrating thoroughly—only then can one reach it; therefore it is not what our sort can attain.
translations.idiomatic: Attaining it comes from spirit penetrating thoroughly—only then can one reach it. Therefore it is not what our sort can attain.

sentences.zh: 且褚侍中澄富貴亦能救人疾，卿此更成不達。

translations.literal: Moreover Attendant Chu Cheng in wealth and nobility can also save people's illnesses—you doing this becomes even more unenlightened.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Attendant Chu Cheng in wealth and nobility can also save people's illnesses—you doing this becomes even more unenlightened.

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「唯達者知此可崇，不達者多以為深累，既鄙之何能不恥之。

translations.literal: " They answered: "Only the enlightened know this can be honored—the unenlightened mostly think it a deep burden; since they despise it, how can one not be ashamed?
translations.idiomatic: " They answered, "Only the enlightened know this can be honored—the unenlightened mostly think it a deep burden. Since they despise it, how can one not be ashamed?

sentences.zh: 」文伯為效與嗣伯相埒。

translations.literal: " Wenbo's efficacy matched Sibo's.
translations.idiomatic: " Wenbo's efficacy matched Sibo's.

sentences.zh: 宋孝武路太后病，眾醫不識。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Lu of Emperor Xiaowu of Song was ill and the host of physicians did not recognize it.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Lu of Emperor Xiaowu of Song was ill and the host of physicians did not recognize it.

sentences.zh: 文伯診之曰：「此石博小腸耳。

translations.literal: Wenbo diagnosed and said: "This is a stone blocking the small intestine.
translations.idiomatic: Wenbo diagnosed and said, "This is a stone blocking the small intestine.

sentences.zh: 」乃為水劑消石湯，病即愈。

translations.literal: " He made a water formula dissolving-stone decoction and the illness was at once cured.
translations.idiomatic: " He made a water formula dissolving-stone decoction and the illness was at once cured.

sentences.zh: 除鄱陽王常侍，遺以千金，旬日恩意隆重。

translations.literal: He was made regular attendant to the Prince of Poyang and given a thousand in gold; within ten days favor was heavy.
translations.idiomatic: He was made regular attendant to the Prince of Poyang and given a thousand in gold. Within ten days favor was heavy.

sentences.zh: 宋明帝宮人患腰痛牽心，每至輒氣欲絕，眾醫以為肉症。

translations.literal: An palace woman of Emperor Ming had back pain pulling at the heart—each time she nearly stopped breathing; the host of physicians thought it a flesh tumor.
translations.idiomatic: A palace woman of Emperor Ming had back pain pulling at the heart—each time she nearly stopped breathing. Physicians thought it a flesh tumor.

sentences.zh: 文伯曰：「此發症。

translations.literal: Wenbo said: "This is hair syndrome.
translations.idiomatic: Wenbo said, "This is hair syndrome.

sentences.zh: 」以油投之，即吐得物如發。

translations.literal: " With oil administered she at once vomited up something like hair.
translations.idiomatic: " With oil administered she at once vomited up something like hair.

sentences.zh: 稍引之長三尺，頭已成蛇能動，掛門上適盡一發而已，病都差。

translations.literal: Drawing it out little by little it was three chi long; the head had already become a snake able to move—hung on the door it was exactly one full head of hair and the illness was wholly cured.
translations.idiomatic: Drawing it out little by little it was three chi long. The head had already become a snake able to move—hung on the door it was exactly one full head of hair and the illness was wholly cured.

sentences.zh: 宋後廢帝出樂游苑門，逢一婦人有娠，帝亦善診，診之曰：「此腹是女也。

translations.literal: Emperor Fei of Song later went out the Leyou Park gate and met a pregnant woman—the Emperor also skilled in diagnosis, diagnosed and said: "This belly is a girl.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Fei of Song later went out the Leyou Park gate and met a pregnant woman. The emperor also skilled in diagnosis said, "This belly is a girl.

sentences.zh: 」問文伯，曰：「腹有兩子，一男一女，男左邊，青黑，形小於女。

translations.literal: " He asked Wenbo, who said: "The belly holds two children, one male one female—the male on the left, green-black, form smaller than the female.
translations.idiomatic: " He asked Wenbo, who said, "The belly holds two children, one male one female—the male on the left, green-black, smaller than the female.

sentences.zh: 」帝性急，便欲使剖。

translations.literal: " The Emperor's nature was urgent and he at once wished to cut open.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor's nature was urgent and he at once wished to cut open.

sentences.zh: 文伯惻然曰：「若刀斧恐其變異，請針之立落。

translations.literal: Wenbo said with compassion: "If knife and axe I fear mutation—please needle and they will fall at once.
translations.idiomatic: Wenbo said with compassion, "If knife and axe I fear mutation—please needle and they will fall at once.

sentences.zh: 」便寫足太陰，補手陽明，胎便應針而落。

translations.literal: " He then wrote on the foot Taiyin and supplemented the hand Yangming—the fetus responded to the needles and fell.
translations.idiomatic: " He wrote on the foot Taiyin and supplemented the hand Yangming—the fetus responded to the needles and fell.

sentences.zh: 兩兒相續出，如其言。

translations.literal: The two children came out one after another as he had said.
translations.idiomatic: The two children came out one after another as he had said.

sentences.zh: 子雄亦傳家業，尤工診察，位奉朝請。

translations.literal: His son Xiong also transmitted the family craft and was especially skilled in diagnosis, serving as gentleman who attends court.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xiong also transmitted the family craft and was especially skilled in diagnosis, serving as gentleman who attends court.

sentences.zh: 能清言，多為貴遊所善。

translations.literal: Able in pure talk, he was much favored by the noble and wandering.
translations.idiomatic: Able in pure talk, he was much favored by the noble and wandering.

sentences.zh: 事母孝謹，母終，毀瘠幾至自滅。

translations.literal: He served his mother with filial care; when his mother died he wasted away nearly to self-extinction.
translations.idiomatic: He served his mother with filial care. When his mother died he wasted away nearly to self-extinction.

sentences.zh: 俄而兄亡，扶杖臨喪，撫膺一慟，遂以哀卒。

translations.literal: Soon his elder brother also died; leaning on a staff at the funeral he beat his chest once in grief and died of sorrow.
translations.idiomatic: Soon his elder brother also died. Leaning on a staff at the funeral he beat his chest once in grief and died of sorrow.

sentences.zh: 嗣伯字叔紹，亦有孝行，善清言，位正員郎，諸府佐，彌為臨川王映所重。

translations.literal: Sibo, styled Shushao, also had filial conduct, was skilled in pure talk, served as regular gentleman, staff of various headquarters, and was especially valued by Prince Ying of Linchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Sibo, styled Shushao, also had filial conduct and pure talk, served as regular gentleman and various staff posts, and was especially valued by Prince Ying of Linchuan.

sentences.zh: 時直合將軍房伯玉服五石散十許劑，無益，更患冷，夏日常復衣。

translations.literal: At that time Direct-office General Fang Boyu had taken five-stone powder for ten-odd doses without benefit and instead suffered cold— in summer he often wore padded clothes.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Direct-office General Fang Boyu had taken five-stone powder for ten-odd doses without benefit and instead suffered cold—in summer he often wore padded clothes.

sentences.zh: 嗣伯為診之，曰：「卿伏熱，應須以水發之，非冬月不可。

translations.literal: Sibo diagnosed and said: "You harbor latent heat and should need water to release it—not possible except in winter.
translations.idiomatic: Sibo diagnosed and said, "You harbor latent heat and need water to release it—not possible except in winter.

sentences.zh: 」至十一月，冰雪大盛，令二人夾捉伯玉，解衣坐石，取冷水從頭澆之，盡二十斛。

translations.literal: " In the eleventh month ice and snow were great; he had two men hold Boyu on either side, stripped him to sit on stone, and poured cold water from the head—altogether twenty hu.
translations.idiomatic: " In the eleventh month ice and snow were great. He had two men hold Boyu, stripped him to sit on stone, and poured cold water from the head—altogether twenty hu.

sentences.zh: 伯玉口噤氣絕，家人啼哭請止。

translations.literal: Boyu's mouth clenched and breath stopped—the family wept and begged to stop.
translations.idiomatic: Boyu's mouth clenched and breath stopped—the family wept and begged to stop.

sentences.zh: 嗣伯遣人執杖防合，敢有諫者撾之。

translations.literal: Sibo sent men with staves to guard the gate—whoever dared remonstrate would be beaten.
translations.idiomatic: Sibo sent men with staves to guard the gate—whoever dared remonstrate would be beaten.

sentences.zh: 又盡水百斛，伯玉始能動，而見背上彭彭有氣。

translations.literal: Again altogether one hundred hu of water—Boyu then could move and saw swelling on his back like rising breath.
translations.idiomatic: Again altogether one hundred hu of water—Boyu then could move and saw swelling on his back like rising breath.

sentences.zh: 俄而起坐，曰：「熱不可忍，乞冷飲。

translations.literal: Soon he rose and sat and said: "The heat is unbearable—beg cold drink.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he rose and said, "The heat is unbearable—beg cold drink.

sentences.zh: 」嗣伯以水與之，一飲一升，病都差。

translations.literal: " Sibo gave him water—one drink one sheng—and the illness was wholly cured.
translations.idiomatic: " Sibo gave him water—one drink one sheng—and the illness was wholly cured.

sentences.zh: 自爾恒發熱，冬月猶單褌衫，體更肥壯。

translations.literal: From then he always ran fever; in winter he still wore single trousers and shirt and his body grew still more robust.
translations.idiomatic: From then he always ran fever. In winter he still wore single trousers and shirt and his body grew still more robust.

sentences.zh: 常有嫗人患滯冷，積年不差。

translations.literal: There was once an old woman with lingering cold—not cured for years.
translations.idiomatic: There was once an old woman with lingering cold—not cured for years.

sentences.zh: 嗣伯為診之曰：「此屍注也，當取死人枕煮服之乃愈。

translations.literal: Sibo diagnosed and said: "This is corpse-injection; one must take a dead man's pillow, boil and take it—then one will recover.
translations.idiomatic: Sibo diagnosed and said, "This is corpse-injection. One must take a dead man's pillow, boil and take it—then one will recover.

sentences.zh: 」於是往古塚中取枕，枕已一邊腐缺，服之即差。

translations.literal: " He then went to an ancient tomb and took a pillow—one side already rotted away—and on taking it she recovered at once.
translations.idiomatic: " He went to an ancient tomb and took a pillow—one side already rotted away—and on taking it she recovered at once.

sentences.zh: 後秣陵人張景，年十五，腹脹面黃，眾醫不能療，以問嗣伯。

translations.literal: Later Zhang Jing of Moling, age fifteen, had swollen belly and yellow face—the host of physicians could not cure; they asked Sibo.
translations.idiomatic: Later Zhang Jing of Moling, age fifteen, had swollen belly and yellow face—physicians could not cure; they asked Sibo.

sentences.zh: 嗣伯曰：「此石蚘耳，極難療。

translations.literal: Sibo said: "This is stone roundworm—extremely hard to treat.
translations.idiomatic: Sibo said, "This is stone roundworm—extremely hard to treat.

sentences.zh: 當取死人枕煮之。

translations.literal: One must take a dead man's pillow and boil it.
translations.idiomatic: One must take a dead man's pillow and boil it.

sentences.zh: 」依語煮枕，以湯投之，得大利，並蚘蟲頭堅如石，五升，病即差。

translations.literal: " Following the words they boiled the pillow and poured in the decoction—obtained great benefit, and roundworm heads hard as stone, five sheng—the illness was at once cured.
translations.idiomatic: " They boiled the pillow and poured in the decoction—obtained great benefit, and roundworm heads hard as stone, five sheng—the illness was at once cured.

sentences.zh: 後沈僧翼患眼痛，又多見鬼物，以問嗣伯。

translations.literal: Later Shen Sengyi had eye pain and also often saw ghostly things—they asked Sibo.
translations.idiomatic: Later Shen Sengyi had eye pain and often saw ghostly things—they asked Sibo.

sentences.zh: 嗣伯曰：「邪氣入肝，可覓死人枕煮服之。

translations.literal: Sibo said: "Evil qi has entered the liver—one may seek a dead man's pillow, boil and take it.
translations.idiomatic: Sibo said, "Evil qi has entered the liver. Seek a dead man's pillow, boil and take it.

sentences.zh: 竟，可埋枕於故處。

translations.literal: When finished, bury the pillow in the former place.
translations.idiomatic: When finished, bury the pillow in the former place.

sentences.zh: 」如其言又愈。

translations.literal: " Following his words he again recovered.
translations.idiomatic: " Following his words he again recovered.

sentences.zh: 王晏問之曰：「三病不同，而皆用死人枕而俱差，何也？

translations.literal: Wang Yan asked: "Three illnesses differ yet all used dead men's pillows and all recovered—why?
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yan asked, "Three illnesses differ yet all used dead men's pillows and all recovered—why?

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「屍注者，鬼氣伏而未起，故令人沈滯。

translations.literal: " He answered: "Corpse-injection means ghost qi lies dormant and has not yet risen, therefore making one sunken and stagnant.
translations.idiomatic: " He answered, "Corpse-injection means ghost qi lies dormant and has not yet risen, therefore making one sunken and stagnant.

sentences.zh: 得死人枕投之，魂氣飛越，不得復附體，故屍注可差。

translations.literal: Getting a dead man's pillow and administering it—the soul's qi flies beyond and can no longer attach to the body; therefore corpse-injection can be cured.
translations.idiomatic: Getting a dead man's pillow and administering it—the soul's qi flies beyond and can no longer attach to the body. Therefore corpse-injection can be cured.

sentences.zh: 石蚘者久蚘也，醫療既僻，蚘蟲轉堅，世間藥不能遣，所以須鬼物驅之然後可散，故令煮死人枕也。

translations.literal: Stone roundworm means long-standing roundworm—the medical treatment already remote, the worms turn hard; worldly medicines cannot dispel them, therefore one must use ghost things to drive them before they can scatter; therefore one boils a dead man's pillow.
translations.idiomatic: Stone roundworm means long-standing worms—medical treatment already remote, the worms turn hard. Worldly medicines cannot dispel them, so one must use ghost things to drive them before they scatter. Therefore one boils a dead man's pillow.

sentences.zh: 夫邪氣入肝，故使眼痛而見魍魎，應須而邪物以鉤之，故用死人枕也。

translations.literal: Evil qi entering the liver therefore makes eye pain and one sees wangliang—one should use an evil thing to hook it; therefore one uses a dead man's pillow.
translations.idiomatic: Evil qi entering the liver makes eye pain and one sees wangliang—one should use an evil thing to hook it. Therefore one uses a dead man's pillow.

sentences.zh: 氣因枕去，故令埋於塚間也。

translations.literal: The qi follows the pillow away—therefore one has it buried among the tombs.
translations.idiomatic: The qi follows the pillow away—therefore one has it buried among the tombs.

sentences.zh: 」又春月出南籬門戲，聞笪屋中有呻吟聲。

translations.literal: " Again in spring he went out the southern hedge gate to play and heard groaning in a bamboo house.
translations.idiomatic: " Again in spring he went out the southern hedge gate to play and heard groaning in a bamboo house.

sentences.zh: 嗣伯曰：「此病甚重，更二日不療必死。

translations.literal: Sibo said: "This illness is very severe—in two more days without treatment she will die.
translations.idiomatic: Sibo said, "This illness is very severe—in two more days without treatment she will die.

sentences.zh: 」乃往視，見一老姥稱體痛，而處處有黑敢黑無數。

translations.literal: " He then went to look and saw an old woman saying her body hurt—and everywhere were countless black spots.
translations.idiomatic: " He went to look and saw an old woman saying her body hurt—everywhere countless black spots.

sentences.zh: 嗣伯還煮鬥余湯送令服之，服訖痛勢愈甚，跳投床者無數。

translations.literal: Sibo returned and boiled leftover bean decoction and sent it for her to take—when finished the pain grew still worse and she jumped off the bed countless times.
translations.idiomatic: Sibo returned and boiled leftover bean decoction and sent it for her to take. When finished the pain grew worse and she jumped off the bed countless times.

sentences.zh: 須臾所黑處皆拔出釘，長寸許。

translations.literal: In a moment from every black place nails were pulled out, one cun long.
translations.idiomatic: In a moment from every black place nails were pulled out, one cun long.

sentences.zh: 以膏塗諸瘡口，三日而復，云：「此名釘疽也」。

translations.literal: Ointment was applied to the sores; in three days she recovered, saying: "This is called nail-sore."
translations.idiomatic: Ointment was applied to the sores. In three days she recovered, saying, "This is called nail-sore."

sentences.zh: 時又有薛伯宗善徙癰疽，公孫泰患背，伯宗為氣封之，徙置齋前柳樹上。

translations.literal: At that time there was also Xue Bozong skilled at transferring carbuncles and sores—Gongsun Tai had one on his back; Bozong sealed it with qi and transferred it before the study hall willow tree.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Xue Bozong was also skilled at transferring carbuncles and sores. Gongsun Tai had one on his back. Bozong sealed it with qi and transferred it to the study hall willow tree.

sentences.zh: 明旦癰消，樹邊便起一瘤如拳大。

translations.literal: The next dawn the sore was gone and beside the tree a lump like a fist had risen.
translations.idiomatic: The next dawn the sore was gone and beside the tree a lump like a fist had risen.

sentences.zh: 稍稍長二十餘日，瘤大膿爛，出黃赤汁鬥餘，樹為之痿損。

translations.literal: Gradually over twenty-odd days the lump grew large, pus and rot flowed, yielding yellow-red juice of more than a dou—the tree was withered and damaged thereby.
translations.idiomatic: Gradually over twenty-odd days the lump grew large, pus and rot flowed, yielding yellow-red juice of more than a dou—the tree withered and was damaged.

sentences.zh: 論曰：有晉自宅淮海，張氏無乏賢良。

translations.literal: Commentary says: From Jin's dwelling in the Huai-Hai region the Zhang clan never lacked worthy men.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: From Jin's dwelling in the Huai-Hai region the Zhang clan never lacked worthy men.

sentences.zh: 及宋齊之間，雅道彌盛。

translations.literal: Through Song and Qi the refined Way grew ever more flourishing.
translations.idiomatic: Through Song and Qi the refined Way grew ever more flourishing.

sentences.zh: 其前則雲敷、演、鏡、暢，蓋其尤著者也。

translations.literal: Before them were Fu, Yan, Jing, and Chang—these were especially eminent.
translations.idiomatic: Before them were Fu, Yan, Jing, and Chang—these were especially eminent.

sentences.zh: 然景胤敬愛之道，少微立履所由，其殆優矣。

translations.literal: Yet Jingyin's reverent love and Shaowei's conduct and standing—perhaps they were superior.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Jingyin's reverent love and Shaowei's conduct and standing—perhaps they were superior.

sentences.zh: 思光行己卓越，非常俗所遵，齊高帝所云：「不可有二，不可無一」，斯言其幾得矣。

translations.literal: Siguang's self-conduct was transcendent, not what common custom follows; what Emperor Gao of Qi said—"cannot be two, cannot be without one"—that saying nearly hits the mark.
translations.idiomatic: Siguang's self-conduct was transcendent, not what common custom follows. What Emperor Gao of Qi said—"cannot be two, cannot be without one"—that saying nearly hits the mark.

sentences.zh: 徐氏妙理通靈，蓋非常所至，雖古之和、鵲，何以加茲。

translations.literal: The Xu clan's subtle principles linked with spirits—surely not what the ordinary reaches; though the ancients Bian Que and Cang Gong, how add to this?
translations.idiomatic: The Xu clan's subtle principles linked with spirits—surely beyond the ordinary. Though the ancients Bian Que and Cang Gong, how add to this?

sentences.zh: 融與文伯款好，故附之云爾。

translations.literal: Rong and Wenbo were on warm terms—therefore they are appended here.
translations.idiomatic: Rong and Wenbo were on warm terms—therefore they are appended here.
